On a picturesque hillside in Slovenia, 32-year-old Karam Nwilati is preparing for the ultimate declaration of love. Nervously, he gets down on one knee and opens an engagement ring box. Inside are three rings.

Nwilati is not proposing to one person, but two: his best friends and platonic life partners, Kristian Naydenov, 29, and Santeri Lehtonen, 36. There’s one ring for each of them.

For Naydenov and Lehtonen, the answer was always going to be yes. The three of them have lived together in Berlin since the Covid-19 lockdown, and they have spent the past four-and-a-half years building a community that exists outside conventional relationship ideals. Their “friendship wedding,” a non-legally binding ceremony celebrating their commitment to each other, is planned for October, when they’ll gather their closest friends on the roof of their Berlin apartment.

Nwilati, a content creator, shared a video of the engagement online, which has now received more than 480,000 likes. The reactions have been mixed – the more negative ones ranging from judgmental to hateful – while others have hailed their unconventional relationship as an antidote to the so-called male loneliness epidemic, marked by a rise in social isolation, shrinking friendship circles, and a lack of emotional support among men.

To Nwilati, Naydenov and Lehtonen, friendships are often treated too casually for the depth they can hold. “We don’t celebrate friendships enough,” says Nwilati. “If there’s a friendship breakup, people just kind of fade away without saying anything. It's not like a romantic breakup where you actually have to go through the process of doing.”

open image in gallery Karam Nwilati proposed to his two best friends on a bikepacking trip in Slovenia, and now they’re getting married as platonic life partners ( Kristian Naydenov @thehumanchris / Santeri Lehtonen @santhur )

Women are more likely to celebrate their female friendships publicly – that was the moral of Sex and the City, anyway – yet we rarely see men expressing that same affection so openly. “There’s a lot of masculine posturing involved,” says Lehtonen, a sustainability consultant and activist, as he looks back at his male friendships over the years. “There was a lot of ‘Who’s the man’ and basic male behaviors that didn’t always feel awesome.”

For Lehtonen, the engagement symbolizes a promise and accountability in their friendship, which has become his central support system since they started living together. “I feel like I could call them on the rainiest day on the planet, and even if they’re 20 kilometers away, they would be there to help me with something heavy or to be a shoulder to cry on.”

Often, cohabiting with your friends in your twenties and thirties is considered a waiting room until you find a serious romantic partner to settle down with. It’s not something you typically invest in. In his proposal, Nwilati thanked his friends for being his safe space and home. “I love you…We’re such a beautiful unit. We’re building such an intentional life together,” he said.

It’s a far cry from conventional masculine friendships, where fist bumps are generally preferred to hugs. When men do connect, it is often through group activities rather than one-on-one relationships, according to the American Institute for Boys and Men, which makes it harder to have meaningful, deep conversations.

open image in gallery Santeri Lehtonen, Karam Nwilati and Kristian Naydenov say that friendships are too casual for the depth that they hold ( Kristian Naydenov )

open image in gallery On social media, people have hailed the trio’s unconventional relationship as an antidote to the so-called male loneliness epidemic ( Karam Nwilati @karamintheworld )

“I’ve just seen the alternative [types of friendships], and I think, ‘No thank you,’” says Nwilati. “It comes down to the emotional intimacy that we have with each other. Once you see it and once you experience it, like, there is no other option.”

Lehtonen is the only person out of the trio who is in a romantic relationship. Their friendship is strictly platonic (Lehtonen identifies as bi-curious while the other two are heterosexual), but both Nwilati and Naydenov say that their support system makes single life easier. It also helps them reframe their priorities when they’re dating.

“In society, a romantic partner is painted as someone who should be your best friend and your therapist, and everything in between,” says Nwilati. “And so having these relationships takes off a lot of pressure and creates a healthier base to stand on because I’m not looking for someone to fill a hole – you can meet them for who they are and build on that.” He acknowledges, of course, that there are some things the friendship doesn’t fulfill, such as sexual intimacy, “which obviously we're not exploring in these relationships.”

The unconventional nature of their public declaration of love has not gone unnoticed. Naydenov said his family members have been understanding and supportive, but some will struggle to comprehend it. His mother, he says, understandably had lots of questions. “She was definitely questioning it because she's, like, ‘So, what kind of obligations are you now tied to? What kind of promise do you have to make to each other, like with the traditional sense of the word, ‘marriage?’ I said, well, we’re celebrating five years of friendship and celebrating that we’re living in this house together.” Lehtonen said he was apprehensive about telling his parents, but they took it surprisingly well; Nwilati hasn’t told his.

open image in gallery The trio says that the emotional intimacy they’ve developed while living together for the past four-and-a-half years has been a vital support system ( Kristian Naydenov @thehumanchris / Santeri Lehtonen @santhur )

open image in gallery Santeri Lehtonen, Karam Nwilati and Kristian Naydenov are planning a wedding ceremony on their Berlin rooftop for October ( Karam Nwilati @karamintheworld )

It was a friendship proposal, but the gravity of the moment was still real. “I was super shocked when it happened,” says Naydenov. “It feels like your reality is breaking apart. It feels like something you should only have with a very specific person in your life. It reminded me that I’m living such an unconventional life.”

The long-term goal is for the trio to move to a remote home in the countryside and build a community there. “We would love to eventually live as a six: our romantic partners and us,” says Lehtonen. “In my dream situation, we each have romantic partners. It’s a both/and situation.”

For the upcoming wedding, which they’re currently in the process of planning, they plan to incorporate elements from Arab, Greek and Finnish ceremonies as a homage to their respective heritages. Ultimately, they want to pull from traditional tropes to mark the significance of the occasion.

“I like the idea of keeping some of the traditional ceremony things that you get in weddings in this, just as commentary to be like…. romantic relationships have this…why not also friendship weddings?” says Nwilati. “We twist it and make it our own thing.”

“Maybe we all wear veils?” he asks his friend-fiancées. They all laugh.

“And you can reach back out to us after the divorce.”

The UK is expected to return to milder temperatures this week after a weekend of summer-like conditions which saw parts of the country reach the mid-20s on the mercury.

A southerly wind drawing in hot and humid air from the continent saw temperatures pushed up above average on Sunday, as many were treated to sunshine and bright spells.

Conditions are still expected to be warm on Monday, with parts of the south east reaching 24C. But temperatures will fall to closer to the seasonal average on Tuesday as conditions become more changeable throughout the week.

Parts of the country will hit 24C on Monday ( Met Office )

The mercury is expected to fall to highs of around 20C in London and parts of the south, and a much cooler 16C in Manchester and across the north of England, from Tuesday onwards.

It comes after the Met Office this week confirmed the UK has provisionally experienced its hottest summer since records began nearly 150 years ago.

Five heatwaves between May and August left the majority of the country in drought and have sparked wildfires and travel disruption.

The UK recorded a mean average temperature across June, July and August of 16.5C, beating the previous seasonal high of 16.1C set last year, the Met Office said.

The forecaster previously suggested the UK was on course for its hottest summer on record, provided temperatures remained around average for the rest of August, and it is expected the final figures for the month will break the previous record.

The highest temperature recorded this summer was on 13 August at Kew Gardens, when the mercury hit 38.1C.

While this did not beat the all-time highest record, which was measured at 40.3C in Lincolnshire in July 2022, several other records were broken, including a temperature of 37C or higher being recorded on three separate days.

Prior to 2026, temperatures of over 37C had only been recorded nine times in the UK – three of which have occurred this year.

Met Office five day forecast

Changeable through the week ahead.

Today:

Southern and central areas will be largely dry and bright today. Turning more unsettled in the north with blustery rain and gales in places. Feeling warm in the south in the sunny spells, fresher in the north.

Tonight:

A band of rain moves south across England and Wales tonight, turning heavy at times. Blustery showers in the north with strong winds.

Tuesday:

Heavy rain slowly clearing the southeast in the morning. A brighter day for many and feeling fresh. Winds gradually easing in the north, with showers too.

Outlook for Wednesday to Friday:

Drier and brighter on Wednesday with spells of sunshine. Another band of rain then moves in for Thursday, before drier and brighter weather returns on Friday. Temperatures likely around average.

Naval engineer Ilya Espino de Marotta takes the helm Monday as the first woman to lead the Panama Canal administration, stepping into the role at a challenging time for the vital maritime route.

Buoyed by her leadership of the multi-billion-dollar expansion project last decade, Espino moves up from deputy administrator to take full command of the canal. Only three other Panamanians have held the position since the United States handed over the interoceanic waterway in late 1999.

Her appointment to the canal’s top post is already seen as a symbol of women's capability for executive leadership roles in the industry. The canal serves as the engine of the Panamanian economy and handles nearly 3% of global maritime trade.

Shortly before taking office, Espino told The Associated Press that her priority would be advancing the project to build a reservoir on the Indio River within the canal’s watershed. The $1.5 billion project aims to secure drinking water for 50% of the Central American nation’s 4 million people and to support the future operation of the canal, opened by the U.S. in 1914.

The canal’s Board of Directors had previously appointed her to lead this $1.5 billion plan, which encompasses community resettlement and environmental considerations. It is the largest project since the waterway’s expansion, which opened in June 2016 at a cost exceeding $5.25 billion. Officials expect the reservoir to be completed by late 2031 or 2032.

For Espino, the goal is to guarantee future water supplies without compromising reliability in the eyes of the shipping industry. If customers perceive that the canal is not seeking a long-term water solution, they could shift their cargo to other routes.

That project, which has sparked protests from certain communities, is taking on greater significance as the canal faces another period of low rainfall caused by the El Niño phenomenon, which recently led waterway authorities to restrict the number of ships making the daily crossing between the Atlantic and the Pacific.

Geopolitical tensions for the canal with the US under Trump

As the second-highest-ranking official at the canal serving under outgoing administrator Ricaurte Vásquez, she experienced the tension caused by complaints and warnings regarding the waterway voiced by U.S. President Donald Trump both before and after he assumed office.

Trump threatened to retake control of the canal, citing Chinese influence over the waterway and claiming that U.S. shipping companies were being treated unfairly.

The country’s judiciary ruled unconstitutional the port concessions at both entrances held by a Hong Kong consortium. That ruling followed the announcement of a planned acquisition of those and other ports by a U.S. investment fund, a deal that has since stalled.

Espino told the AP that her responsibility over the next seven years at the helm of the canal will be to maintain operations that are “efficient, neutral, and transparent.” She said that diplomatic matters are the responsibility of the Panamanian state.

Police are hunting to identify offenders after police were injured and cars were damaged in anti-migration protests.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight police said on Monday that “a number of police, Coastguard and Border Force vehicles were damaged” after hundreds of far-right demonstrators descended on Portsmouth.

“A small number of officers were treated at the scene for injuries, but no-one in attendance from any agency or the public was seriously injured.”

They said no arrests have been made at this time, however they had launched an investigation to identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles, or other criminal offences.

It comes after Reform UK chairman Lee Anderson urged those attending protests to “do it the right way” and condemned “attacks on our police”.

He said: “If you’re going to protest then be careful, do it the right way then you have my full support because the left are just looking for an excuse to label you all as far right thugs. You're not, you are decent patriotic Brits who've had enough.”

The government has meanwhile condemned far-right protesters who blocked roads and faced up to riot police over the weekend as “thuggish and intimidating”.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Antonelli walks on water while Hamilton rages from mountaintop
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick sounding like Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in his first testing period as Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK insisted at Everton that Manchester United have not had a “bad start”. They have had a bad start.

Nobody had used the word “bad”. Carrick still felt the need to interrupt a journalist as they highlighted the fact United have taken four points from nine against Hull, Ipswich and Everton.



That Carrick interjected would suggest his quip betrayed his own true feelings. He cannot believe United have started the campaign well.

When the fixture list was published, Hull, Ipswich and Everton were all borderline gimmes. Beyond the two promoted teams, Everton went into the game amid simmering tension between their owners and supporters after a shambolic deadline day.



David Moyes barely has the manpower for a full squad. Everton were in such disarray they tried to sign Joshua Zirkzee.

And yet Everton were still more attack-minded than United. They had the best chance of the first half and recorded twice as many attempts on target.

As much of a concern as the results are Carrick’s press conferences. Sir Alex Ferguson said he used to play two games a week: a match and a press conference. It is unlikely Carrick is of the same opinion.

Carrick will never utter a quote that is a marmalade dropper and he rarely gives a straight answer.

Nobody is knocking his personality. Carrick is as authentic as he was as a player and part of the appeal to the United power brokers is he is the polar opposite to Ruben Amorim. Especially when dictaphones are placed in front of him.

Carrick’s rhetoric was not an issue when United won 12 from 17 games and lost two last season. There was always a sense that he would have to change tact if or when United hit the skids and he hasn’t.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

On Friday, Carrick was given an easy win: will United strengthen their defence next summer?

“It’s not always as simple as that,” Carrick replied.

Supporters do not want to hear that, never mind journalists. Such compliance evokes memories of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

United have been here before. In 2018, an abrasive Portuguese manager turned on the hierarchy and was jettisoned in favour of a club great who was beside himself to have been given the job.

Toeing the line did not get Solskjaer very far. His tenure ended trophyless.



Carrick is close with Solskjaer. They were teammates, coached together for nearly three years and were up against each other for the job in January.

With 23 years of playing experience at United between them, they share the same worldview. That does not necessarily correspond to a successful United side in this era.

The angriest Solskjaer ever reacted in a press conference was when reminded of Robin van Persie’s comments about him smiling in defeat to Arsenal in January 2020.



Carrick is slightly different. He took umbrage at the suggestion that Middlesbrough supporters would be surprised by his record at United last season: “We did win a few games.”

This season, there was mild annoyance at Jan Aage Fjortoft’s assertion that United lacked “passion” in the opening weekend defeat at Hull. Carrick then took exception to a journalist’s description of a “passive” performance.

United are too passive. They only forced the issue at Everton after half-time and after Everton equalised. So they were spurred into action. That has to change.

So do Carrick’s press conferences. He has said in successive weeks he “didn’t say” things nobody claimed he had said.

It was Carrick who remarked, “The situation is what it is in terms of finances and what we can do.” When the topic returned to United’s finances in relation to the transfer window, Carrick stressed he did not say “restrictions”. That was a guarded response from a guarded personality.



Carrick has got to look after himself at times. United wanted a defender – a left back – in the summer and did not get one. That is not his fault.

The state of United’s defence is mostly on the current regime. They bought Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt and Ayden Heaven before agreeing a new contract with Harry Maguire. Noussair Mazraoui was also signed on Ineos’s watch.

Nobody is expecting Carrick to cut loose and question his paymasters. But by volunteering the opinion that United have not had a “bad start”, he is putting himself in the firing line.

Solskjaer refused to deflect attention onto others. Paul Pogba and his late agent Mino Raiola undermined him relentlessly and were probably emboldened by Solskjaer branding Pogba a “heart of gold”.



United players felt Solskjaer was a soft touch. Long after Solskjaer had gone, he admitted the dressing room was teeming with “snowflakes”.

There were glimpses of Carrick becoming a more assertive talker at the training camp in Ireland last month. He said “push” or “pushing” eight times in reference to the need for more signings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Carrick had essentially done no media for three months and there were unanswered questions. It was the best he has spoken since he took over on January 13 and the more relaxed setting at Carton House helped, even with the presence of the Amazon cameras.

He has since regressed and so have United. It has been a bad start.

Sports.title: Inside Fulham’s toxic meltdown as fans chant X-rated abuse at Alvaro Arbeloa and players ‘launch secret protest’
Sports.content:
“WHAT the f***ing hell was that”.

Three games in and a large section of Fulham fans have turned on Alvareo Arbeloa.



That was the chant at full-time from the Hammersmith End after a 3-2 defeat to Crystal Palace, the third Premier League defeat in a row.

Only Coventry are also yet to win a game, and with Liverpool away and Manchester United at home before the extended international break, it won’t be a shock if Fulham are on zero points until the middle of October when they play again.



Perhaps more worryingly for Fulham, there are rumblings that the players are turning on Arbeloa too.

Club record-signing Kevin, an unused substitute at the weekend, tweeted a cryptic image on Instagram of “no hear, no speak, no see”.

Emile Smith-Rowe and Alex Iwobi have removed all photos of themselves related to Fulham from their Instagram.

Kenny Tete, currently being overlooked at right-back with Timothy Castagne preferred, is alleged to have replied to a fan who asked what was going on after Saturday’s match: “Talk to the f***ing manager”.

So are Fulham in meltdown? And how have things turned so toxic so quick?

Fears for the Cottagers started the moment Marco Silva surprised the owners by deciding to walk away to become Benfica manager.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Silva represented stability, experience and was much loved by Fulham fans – a hard act to follow.

So the appointment of Arbeloa, 43, who’s only managerial experience was a mediocre caretaker spell at Real Madrid, always felt like a risk.

The sense of gambling by the River Thames only increased as experienced players Raul Jimenez, Harry Wilson (both out of contract), Issa Diop and Sasa Lukic departed the club – taking their combined 658 Premier League games experience with them.



In their place came Gonzalo Garcia, Shea Charles, David Affenbruger, Cesar Palacios, Jonah Kusi-Asare, Manuel Angel and Hugo Larsson – players with a combined total of EIGHT Prem games under their belts before the season started and an average age of 21 years and 10 months.

Worryingly, the lack of experience has shown. Fulham have looked defensively naive, shipping a goal inside 35 seconds in their opening game to Chelsea and being carved open by Crystal Palace’s LEFT-BACKS on Saturday.

Fulham’s transfer dealings and start to the season have only intensified the fears of fans that Arbeloa is inexperienced and doesn’t know what he’s doing.

Despite a sense of doom at the Cottage, there are positives to take from the start of the season.

Fulham have lost all of their games by one goal. They could have quite easily won or drawn all of them with some better finishing and less stupidity at the back. That they are in games rather than getting hammered is a much better place from where to begin turning things around.



Gonzalo, a striker who made 30 appearances for Real Madrid last term, has at times looked a steal at £34m. His goal against AFC Wimbledon in the League Cup a thing of beauty.

Academy product Josh King looks to have gone up a level, with two goals already this season and a clear standout in the team. His call-up to the England squad before the World Cup, to help the team prepare for the tournament, looks to have given him an extra shot of confidence.

The club brought in three players on deadline day, among them centre-back Affenbruger who Fulham fans will hope offers more pace than the slow and increasingly ponderous Joachim Anderson.



We are just three games into the season, a new manager with a ton of new players can be excused for needing a little time to get his ideas and plan into gear. But many fans seem in no mood to allow that.

What matters to Arbeloa is whether the owners do.

It was American billionaire Shahid Khan who ultimately made the decision to appoint the ex-Liverpool player, with input from his wrestling-loving son Tony, who is Fulham’s Director of Football Operations. Surely they won’t want to admit they got it wrong so quickly.

But on the flip-side they’ve invested millions in the club, most notably upgrading the Riverside Stand into the most plush hospitality experience in the country. They will be only too aware that flogging a £900 ticket to a Championship match vs Lincoln will be a tough sell, however good the Michelin star food is.



There is only so much patience they can afford to show and why Arbeloa has seen his odds of being the next Prem manager to be given the boot cut from 3/1 to 9/4.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fulham always looked in for a tough start to the season, playing three of the “big six” and going away to Sunderland among their first five games. That was the why the defeat to Palace cut deep for Fulham fans – it looked the one clearly “winnable” game.

It looks more likely the run of games after the international break will decide whether Arbeloa has a future at Fulham or not. The Cottagers play Ipswich, Hull and Coventry. Fail to take the majority of points from the three promoted teams, and Fulham fans will be looking back at Arbeloa’s reign, justifiably asking, “what the f***ing hell was that.”

Sports.title: ‘I was screaming’ – Gary Neville slams THREE Man Utd stars for role in Everton equaliser as he reveals ‘fear’ for season
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE has torn into three Manchester United stars over Everton’s late equaliser, admitting he fears the defensive problems could haunt his former club all season.

United surrendered a 2-1 lead at Goodison Park on Sunday as Ainsley Maitland-Niles produced a stunning late strike to earn Everton a 2-2 draw.



The result means United have now conceded twice in each of their opening three Premier League games.

And Neville was furious with the way Michael Carrick‘s side allowed Everton to build the move that eventually led to the equaliser.



The former United defender singled out Leny Yoro, Patrick Dorgu and Andrey Santos for their roles in the defensive collapse.

Neville claimed he was “screaming” at his television as Everton exploited the space down United’s left flank.

His biggest concern is that United could not find a solution even with what he considers their strongest available defence on the pitch.

United started with Luke Shaw, Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez across the back.

But Neville believes the warning signs were there long before Maitland-Niles unleashed his spectacular effort.

He argued that United failed to react quickly enough as Everton moved forward, allowing the hosts to work the ball into a dangerous position.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Neville also questioned the decision-making of the defenders, insisting United should have been more disciplined with the game entering its final stages.

The Sky Sports pundit fears opponents will increasingly believe they can hurt United if the Red Devils continue giving up cheap goals.

United have now conceded six times in three league games-despite having taken four points from those matches.

And Neville believes the problem could become a major issue as the season progresses.

He said on the Gary Neville podcast: “I don’t think it’s going to go away and that’s my big fear.



“That last goal is a really bad one. There’s a lot that happens before that goal goes in the back of Manchester United‘s net.

“When you’re playing against a team, it’s 2-1, you’re away, you’ve got to push up, you’ve got to make sure you don’t have players sprinting off and doing stupid things.

“Dorgu sprints forward, the ball gets played past him and Everton just drift down that left side so easily.



“Santos doesn’t get across and when he doesn’t get across quickly enough Yoro is deep and narrow, almost playing like a third or fourth narrow centre back waiting for the ball to go into the box.

“So they could have stopped it at source. That to me is a real error in the lead-up, and I was screaming as it happened because you know full well you’re going to get the ball pumped into the box and you’re going to get a team behind desperate in the last few minutes so you have to make sure you’re organised and United weren’t organised in that last couple of minutes.’

The former England international added that he did not know how Carrick would solve the problem with limited defensive options available to him.

Matthijs de Ligt remains sidelined with a long-term injury, leaving Carrick short of alternatives in defence.

Neville also questioned late substitutions involving Shaw and Dalot, arguing that repeatedly changing the back four can make an already fragile defence even more unsettled.



United will now have little time to dwell on the Everton result.

They face Azerbaijan side Sabah FK in the Champions League before returning to Premier League action against bitter rivals Manchester City in the Manchester derby.

Carrick was also unhappy with United’s defensive display and admitted his players must improve.



The United boss said when asked about Maitland-Niles’ equaliser.: “Obviously we can’t ignore it.

“We need to concede fewer goals to give us a better chance of winning games.”

There pressure is now on the manager to tighten the back if United are to go on and have a good season.

Sports.title: Arsenal sent Champions League warning as two teams who can stop them named
Sports.content:
You can almost hear the music. The Champions League returns this week, with the third edition of the competition's new format set to get underway on Tuesday.

So far, it's been dominated by one club: Paris Saint-Germain, who narrowly beat Arsenal in last season's final. But will that change this time around?

The five Premier League teams involved will certainly hope so, as Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool vie to lift the trophy in Madrid next June. But as ever, the giants of Europe are out to stop them and claim glory for themselves.

We asked the Mirror Football team to look into their crystal balls and see who they're predicting to go all the way.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

John Cross - Arsenal

This should be Arsenal's year. Mikel Arteta went so close last year and it feels that the Arsenal manager has made wonderful steps of progression throughout his time in charge at the Emirates.

For example, going close in the title race. Then winning it. Progression from quarters into the semis and then just two spot kicks away from glory.

‌



That will give Arteta a sense of frustration but also unfinished business in the Champions League. Arsenal are better this season - though the forward line at the highest level might be an issue as it was last year - and will feel they can go one better.

I also really think Bayern Munich are such a force. You can tell that Harry Kane wants more and believes he can win it.

Bayern have gone closer, they have the best striker in the world right now and I feel as if it could come down to Arsenal or Bayern with Barcelona fast improving.

Who'll win the 2026-27 Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Arsenal have never won the Champions League (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Andy Dunn - Barcelona

Considering Premier League clubs spent £3.49billion on players in the summer transfer window, you would hope one of their number emerges as Europe's top dog. But despite all the cash lavished by England's contenders, that is not going to happen.

Arsenal went close last season and will be hard to beat but have they improved enough to be the dominant European force? No. Are Manchester City a step-up on last season? No. The same goes for the rest of the Premier League representatives.

The Champions League winner will come from one of four: Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich. These are the clubs with the stellar names who can decide the biggest games. The ones who produce when needed.

‌



Of those stellar names, the one who will light up this season's Champions League is Lamine Yamal. And that is why Barcelona will win their sixth European Cup.

View 5 Images Lamine Yamal and Raphinha have started the season on fire for Barcelona (Image: Lluis GENE/AFP via Getty Images)

Jeremy Cross - PSG

This sounds predictable and boring, but it's difficult to see past the might of Paris Saint-Germain. Having won the Champions League back-to-back, the French giants will be on a mission to repeat what Real Madrid once did and make it a hat-trick of titles.

After all those years of trying, the European monkey is well and truly off their backs. And despite selling some players this summer, Luis Enrique's men still have loads of world-class talent and now know what it takes to land the biggest cub prize of them all.

‌



Someone is going to have to try to stop them - but I just can't see this happening.

View 5 Images Bayern Munich lost to Paris Saint-Germain in last season's semi-finals (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

Nathan Ridley - Arsenal

Quarter-finalists, semi-finalists, finalists, winners? Arsenal have been on a steady upward trajectory over the past three years and you'd be foolish at this point to write them off.

The Gunners were a couple of penalties away from beating Paris Saint-Germain, who they contained like no other side managed to in the knockout stages. Although it's early days, PSG don't look the same force this season while Arsenal better in attack and as solid defensively despite multiple injuries.

‌



Bayern Munich should go far, as will Barcelona, but their defences just aren't up to scratch. It'll be interesting to see how Manchester City and Liverpool get on under Enzo Maresca and Andoni Iraola respectively, and Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid should provide a compelling storyline at the very least.

But for me, Arsenal look the best-equipped side to be crowned European champions for the first time in their history.

View 5 Images Jose Mourinho is back at Real Madrid and knows how to win the Champions League (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Daniel Orme - Arsenal

The Gunners finally got over the line when it comes to the Premier League and this year might just be the year they finally get their hands on a European crown.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side have it all; they've got the best defence in Europe, their midfield could rival any club and they're more than capable of scoring goals. And one bonus that Arsenal have is their ability to get over the line in big games.

It's just a shame that from their perspective the one they weren't able to came in the Champions League final last season. That should stand them in good stead this season - and give them that hunger this time around.

When it comes to their competition, Real Madrid, Manchester City and Liverpool are in transition. PSG also do not seem as imperious as last season, albeit do not bet against them improving as the season goes on.

Barcelona and Bayern Munich will give Arteta some headaches but neither of those have reached finals since 2015 and 2020 respectively, so are not the European powerhouses that they once were.

‌

Sports.title: Harry Kane MUST win Ballon d'Or and end England's 25-year hoodoo
Sports.content:
It is incredible that English football has not had a Ballon D’Or winner in 25 years. But the long wait has to end because there can be no more deserving winner than Harry Kane.

For Kane to score 73 goals for club and country across a single season is an astonishing achievement. Yes, in a World Cup year, the winner normally comes from the team which lifts the World Cup.

But, in my view, Kane presents a more compelling case as an individual ahead of even Spain’s squad of World Cup winners. Rodri was Spain’s most important player in the tournament and, over the course of 12 months, Kane has done more.

The last English winner was Michael Owen in 2001 and the former Real Madrid star has even backed Kane to get the Ballon D’Or and join the “exclusive club.”

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Quite right, too. You will be familiar by now that I love Jude Bellingham and he finished third two years ago. He was brilliant at the World Cup and was surely England’s best player.

However, Kane did captain England to third place (their best ever finish on foreign soil) and scored six goals in the World Cup.

But, again, over the course of the year, it is Kane who was consistent, scored an incredible amount of goals, won the Bundesliga, the Super Cup and the German Cup.

‌



He was comfortably the top scorer in Europe, outshone the likes of Ousmane Dembele for the Champions League winners and was way more prolific than Kylian Mbappe.

View 2 Images Kane has enjoyed a stellar 12 months for club and country

His all-round game has never been better as he drops deep, links play and is a great leader for club and country. Let’s not forget the Ballon d'Or criteria are:

Individual performances, decisive and impressive character Team performances and achievements Class and fair play. Kane fits with all of those things. He is a class act. Brilliant team and individual player. His achievements are off the scale.

‌



One thing we don’t hear enough about is his passion and hard work for charity, his foundation, giving back for the community and his affection for his upbringing and roots.

Harry Kane targets Ballon d'Or, Champions League and England glory in bold career statement READ MORE :

Champions League is back — get your Road to Madrid special now READ MORE :

Kane is the epitome of the model pro. He dreams of these achievements and emulating the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.

This is his time. And there’s something else. It has gone slightly under the radar that the Ballon d’Or ceremony on October 26 is being held in London for the first time.

The famous Théâtre du Châtelet in Paris has hosted in recent years and the organisers have given a nod to the fact it is 70 years since Stanley Matthews won the first award.

‌



Do not be fooled by coincidence. The Ballon d’Or timing and location is done with a purpose. And there should be an open invitation for Harry Kane.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy set for awkward Burnley reunion after fans brutally mocked his wife Rebekah
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy set for awkward Burnley reunion after fans brutally mocked his wife Rebekah

New Burnley man Jamie Vardy will soon reunite with the fanbase who mocked his wife Rebekah as she became embroiled in a high-profile lawsuit

View 3 Images Jamie Vardy was taunted when Leicester City faced Burnley almost seven years ago (Image: Getty)

Jamie Vardy has signed for Burnley on a one-year deal. So he'll have to put a run-in with the Clarets faithful, in which they ridiculed his wife Rebekah, behind him.

‌



Iconic former Leicester City striker Vardy, who helped fire the Foxes to an unlikely Premier League title in 2016 with his 24 top-flight strikes, is back in England. He waved Leicester goodbye in 2025 after their relegation to the Championship and signed for Italian side Cremonese.

‌



The 39-year-old penned a one-year contract and concluded his first and only season in Serie A with seven league goals as his team failed to avoid the drop. Seeking pastures new, Vardy was linked with a handful of English sides this summer, but has landed at Turf Moor as a free agent.

‌



However, Vardy has a history with the fans of his new Championship outfit. In 2019, when Burnley faced Leicester at the King Power Stadium, a chant regarding his wife Rebekah was aimed in his direction.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jamie Vardy finally decides next club as Leicester icon signs one-year deal READ MORE :

8 controversial Mike Dean moments from row with Arsenal manager to celebrating goal READ MORE :

Burnley travelled to Leicester in October 2019, days after Coleen Rooney, wife of England and Manchester United legend Wayne, first publicly alleged that Rebekah was responsible for leaking posts from her private Instagram account to a British tabloid.

‌



View 3 Images Rebekah sued for libel (Image: Getty)

What ensued was a bitter legal case. Rebekah denied the claims and sued Rooney for libel in June 2020. In July 2022, the judge ruled in Rooney's favour, finding it "substantially true" that Rebekah and her agent had routinely passed Rooney's private information to the media. As a result, Rebekah was ordered to pay the majority of Rooney's legal fees.

But before this conclusion, the allegations were fresh, and Burnley fans took it upon themselves to poke fun at Vardy and mock his spouse. During the first half, a chorus from the away section sounded: "Jamie Vardy, your wife is a grass."

‌

Chris Wood gave the Clarets a 1-0 lead in the 26th minute, but Vardy did not take this or the chant lying down. After being serenaded, he scored to level the game on the stroke of half-time and cupped his ears to the Burnley fans, likely indicating he had heard their singing.

Youri Tielemans' 74th-minute strike ensured the home side walked away with all three points, and Vardy was the one laughing last. Now, after putting an end to his 13-year Leicester tenure and a brief spell in Italy, he calls Burnley home.

‌



View 3 Images Vardy headed home the equaliser (Image: Getty)

Vardy's new team currently sit rock-bottom of the Championship on just two points after a dismal start to the season. He is hoping he can help turn their fortunes around.

"I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley FC," Vardy told the club's website. "This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town. I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction."

Head Coach Nicky Hayen added: "We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley FC. His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign. Jamie has a proven track record and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt."

Sports.title: Arsenal given new Gabriel red card verdict after Chelsea incident - 'Extremely lucky'
Sports.content:
Arsenal given new Gabriel red card verdict after Chelsea incident - 'Extremely lucky'

Gabriel caught Emi Martinez with his foot during a goalmouth scramble in the first half of Arsenal's 2-1 win against Chelsea, but the defender escaped punishment from VAR

View 2 Images Gabriel risked a sending off (Image: Sky Sports)

Wayne Rooney believes that Arsenal star Gabriel was 'extremely lucky' to avoid being shown a red card after kicking Emi Martinez in the face. The incident occurred in the first half as Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates on Sunday.

‌



After Chelsea took the lead through Morgan Rogers with 77 seconds on the clock, the hosts went searching for an equaliser. Martin Odegaard's low free-kick resulted in a goalmouth scramble, with Gabriel among the swarm of players looking to win the ball.

‌



While on the ground, the Arsenal defender flung out his leg but only caught a fraction of the ball. His left foot hit Martinez's head and the Chelsea goalkeeper needed treatment.

‌



No foul was given by referee Chris Kavanagh and VAR decided not to intervene, yet Rooney reckons that Gabriel should've seen red. On Match of the Day, the Manchester United legend said: "You don't really see it at first sight but then when you see a replay and they slow it down.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Martinez has got the ball in his hands and Gabriel boots him in the head, he swings a leg and goes way over the top. He's extremely lucky to stay on the pitch."

Fellow pundit Ashley Young added: "I agree. When the ball is on the floor and Martinez has it, Gabriel kicks so high. I'm not sure why it hasn't gone to VAR of if they've properly studied it because he's nowhere the ball. He's got away with one there."

Arsenal did soon equalise through Kai Havertz before Odegaard fired them into the lead shortly after half-time. Chelsea couldn't find a response and went home empty-handed, with the Gabriel incident emerging as a major talking point following the London derby.

‌



Should Gabriel have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Emi Martinez needed treatment after he was caught (Image: Sky Sports)

However, former Premier League referee Mark Halsey disagrees with Rooney and Young, telling the Sun: "Everybody was on the floor. There's legs flying all over the place, and then there was the ball was loose and Gabriel aims a kick at the ball, totally misses the ball, and then catches Chelsea goalkeeper Martinez in the head.

‌



"Now, is that an act of violent conduct or is it, was it normal contact? Yes, for me, I think there's a doubt there to whether it was violent conduct, only Gabriel will know if he deliberately kicked Martinez.

"But for me, without a doubt, it's not violent conduct because everybody's in there. He's got a right to go for the ball and because they're all on the floor, that's why he's caught Martinez in the head."

Sports.title: Emi Martinez escorted out of Emirates Stadium after Arsenal's win over Chelsea
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez escorted out of Emirates Stadium after Arsenal's win over Chelsea

Emi Martinez appeared to be escorted out of the Emirates Stadium after Chelsea's defeat to Arsenal on Sunday evening

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard shoots past Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez appeared to be escorted out of the Emirates Stadium by bodyguards after his side’s defeat to Arsenal. The Blues were on the receiving end of a 2-1 defeat to the Gunners in the Premier League clash on Sunday afternoon.

‌



Summer signing Morgan Rogers gave Chelsea the lead in the first minute, but Arsenal responded with goals from Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard to secure all three points in North London.

‌



Riccardo Calafiori also had a goal disallowed for Arsenal for an offside just a few minutes after Rogers had opened the scoring for Chelsea.

‌



Martinez was making his return to the Emirates for what was his second appearance for Chelsea after completing a permanent move from Aston Villa earlier in the summer, with the deal believed to be worth around £7.5million.

Alan Shearer makes Enzo Maresca sack claim after Man City 115 charges message READ MORE :

The Argentina international spent 10 years with the Gunners before leaving North London to move to Villa Park back in 2020.

Footage has emerged on social media taken on Sunday evening showing Martinez leave the Emirates and walk through the streets of North London.

‌



The video appeared to show Martinez being accompanied by two bodyguards as they helped the Chelsea shot-stopper get safely past the crowd of fans that had spotted him outside the stadium.

The defeat to Arsenal marks the first loss that Chelsea have suffered this season under new manager Xabi Alonso, but the Blues have already been told why the signing of Martinez will prove to be a good piece of business.

Jamie Redknapp was quizzed during Sky Sports’ coverage of Ipswich Town vs Liverpool on Friday night about whether Brentford star Mamadou Sangare could be the signing of the summer.

‌



View 2 Images Emi Martinez being escorted out of the Emirates Stadium by bodyguards (Image: X / @lumansijohn1)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In response, Redknapp said: "Yeah for me, and also Emi Martinez as well, that was a really smart one,” he said.

‌



“You couldn't take Chelsea seriously this season if they kept the goalkeeper [Robert Sanchez] in place. Not that I don't think he's going to come back and have a really good career, maybe just not at Chelsea.

“But that Emi Martinez one with his experience and quality that he possesses, I think it gives Chelsea a really good chance.

“That's the question mark that everyone had against them: 'Is the goalkeeper good enough?' and he certainly is."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso admits 'I’m not going to go there' when quizzed on Chelsea absentee
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso admits 'I’m not going to go there' when quizzed on Chelsea absentee

Xabi Alonso slipped to his first Chelsea defeat against Arsenal on Sunday afternoon and the Blues boss was without one of his key players for the trip to the Emirates Stadium

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has offered an admission over Moises Caicedo's fitness (Image: Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso admits he made a mistake with Moises Caicedo, having been without the midfielder for the clash with Arsenal. The Blues took on their London rivals on Sunday afternoon, slipping to a 2-1 defeat.

‌



Morgan Rogers had given Chelsea the lead, only for Arsenal to turn the game around via Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard. Xabi Alonso was without key midfielder Caicedo for the game.

‌



The Ecuadorian has endured a frustrating start to the season, having missed the opening day win against Fulham. He returned to make a 14-minute cameo against former club Brighton before being taken off again.

‌



And Alonso has now suggested that his appearance against the Seagulls might have been an error of judgement but has assured that Caicedo is not dealing with a serious issue. The Chelsea boss said: “It is not longer term but it’s about assessing the risk.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“Probably, last week, we took him too early and I don’t want to make the same mistake again. It’s easy after defeats to talk about the players that you are missing.

‌



“I’m not going to go there, I am happy with the players that we have. For sure all the managers need to deal with injuries, with suspensions.

“To have all the players available for all the games is impossible. But we need [Caicedo and Colwill] because they are top players and with them we are a better team.”

Despite having Caicedo out, Alonso was satisfied with the display of his squad, albeit recognised there needs to be improvement.

‌



View 2 Images Caicedo has played just 14 minutes this season (Image: Getty Images)

He said: “I want to compete in the best possible way to win. Today we didn't want to sit deep from the first minute and to wait and to make a long game.

“We wanted to be active, we wanted to be protagonists in the pressing, sometimes to go higher, sometimes lower, to have good possessions. And we have done many right things.

‌



“We need to make it better, we need to learn from them, because this is the top level. When we have to play top level, we want to be as efficient and as accurate in all the phases of the game.

“But this is where we are, this is game three for us of this new start, this new phase that we are starting with Chelsea. But I'm happy with the spirit and the attitude from the players. They have given everything, they have tried and they fought really hard.”

Alonso and Chelsea face another quick turnaround this week, with the Blues scheduled to take on Premier League rivals Leeds in the third round of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer makes Enzo Maresca sack claim after Man City 115 charges message
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer makes Enzo Maresca sack claim after Man City 115 charges message

Alan Shearer has given his verdict on Manchester City's transfer business and their new manager, Enzo Maresca

View 2 Images Alan Shearer has given his verdict on Manchester City (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Alan Shearer has warned that Enzo Maresca’s future at Manchester City could be in doubt if the club fails to win the title. The former Newcastle United striker also expressed confusion about City’s transfer business amid the ongoing charges for an alleged breach of Premier League rules.

‌



City have enjoyed a perfect start to the Premier League this season, winning all three of their opening matches of the season with victories against Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Coventry City.

‌



Those wins currently see City at the top of the Premier League table and one of only two clubs to maintain a 100 percent record, along with current champions Arsenal, who defeated Chelsea on Sunday afternoon at the Emirates.

‌



City have gone into the season with Maresca as their new manager following the departure of Pep Guardiola in the summer after 10 years in charge at the Etihad Stadium.

Gary Neville issues on-air apology as VAR statement released on Arsenal goal vs Chelsea READ MORE :

Shearer, who was speaking before City beat Coventry over the weekend, believes that Maresca’s position as the club’s manager could be under threat if he does not win the title this season.

“You're paying that amount of investment out to win the league,” Shearer told Betfair. “So, City now have to be title challengers.

‌



“And if they don't win the league then I guess the manager would be under huge pressure. You don't spend that money to finish second or third.”

Shearer also weighed in on the 115 charges for allegedly breaching Premier League rules that are still yet to have a verdict, and the seemingly lack of impact it has on City’s transfer business.

View 2 Images Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca (Image: Dave Howarth - CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

City signed Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in deals worth more than £100million each, while Ayyoub Bouaddi was also signed from Lille in a deal reportedly worth up to £86million and Iliman Ndiaye arrived from Everton for around £65million.

“I haven't got a clue how Man City have been able to spend the money they have whilst they are still under those charges,” Shearer said.

‌



“I mean I get why there's so many questions being asked, it's just gone on too long, hasn't it?

“I saw an interview with Richard Masters not so long ago when he said that I understand how everyone views it and looks at it, but he says it's the independent commission decision, so I don't know. I really don't know.”

Manchester United surrendered the lead twice during Sunday's 2-2 draw away to Everton, leaving Michael Carrick's side with four points from their opening three games

View 2 Images Gary Neville was critical of Michael Carrick (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has told Michael Carrick that he can't make the same mistake as his predecessors at Manchester United which led to Sunday's collapse against Everton. The Red Devils were pegged back twice in the dramatic 2-2 draw, as Ainsley Maitland-Niles ultimately denied them with a 96th-minute equaliser.

‌



Both of Everton's goals - the other scored by Tyrique George - were impressive strikes, but Neville believes that both should be scrutinised from his former team's point of view. The ex-United captain couldn't fathom why Carrick subbed both of his full-backs and has a 'big fear' that conceding goals will 'hunt them down the road', having shipped six in their first three games.

‌



Speaking on the Gary Neville Podcast, he bemoaned: "Teams think they've got a chance against them. I thought they were a little bit complacent and I was saying it after the first goal, they lacked that killer instinct before that period when Everton equalised and then they react again.

‌



"Everton weren't at it at all in that first half - United were the better team and didn't have that killer instinct up top and certainly from 1-0 up to 1-1 they let Everton back in the game. It's not going full throttle when you've got a team down, putting them away and then this liability of conceding goals.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I don't think it's going to go away and that's my big fear. I think conceding goals is going to chase them and hunt them down the road and I don't know how Michael deals with it because he's got his best back four on the pitch.

"I don't know why Luke Shaw went off with five minutes to go – hopefully he's not injured. I don't know why Dalot went off with five minutes to go. To be fair, Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag used to change their back four a lot as well.

"You can't be changing your back four. If you've got [Piero] Hincapie to come on for [Riccardo] Calafiori maybe you can, but United have got a back four of Shaw, Dalot, [Harry] Maguire and Lisandro Martinez and they've not got much behind that. So you can't really change your back four at 1-0 or 2-1."

‌



Do you agree with Gary Neville? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has been likened to Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Carrick acknowledged United's defensive frailties post-match, admitting: "Obviously, we can't ignore it. We need to concede fewer goals to give us a better chance of winning games. We'll certainly look at that and keep improving.

‌



"There's obviously things we need to get better at as a team. There's been two strikes from distance really, two really good strikes from their point of view. Sometimes they fly in the top corner and more often than not they probably don't."

United are back in action on Thursday, making their return to the Champions League against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah. Carrick's side will then face Manchester City at Old Trafford this Sunday, where a win could kickstart their 2026-27 campaign.
