Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

José Mourinho congratulated Real Betis for “playing for a draw and then winning the lottery” after his first defeat back as Real Madrid coach. Troy Parrott, given his professional debut by Mourinho at Tottenham, scored his first Betis goal in Friday’s 1-0 win at La Cartuja. Mourinho slumped in his chair as VAR spotted an offside in Carlos Espí’s acrobatic equaliser before Kylian Mbappé had a stoppage-time penalty saved by Álvaro Valles, leaving Barcelona to extend their lead over Madrid to three points with a 5-0 rout of Valencia on Sunday. Luck of the Irish?

Sandwiched between Barça and Madrid are Alavés, who have won three of their first four games. The former Real Madrid striker Mariano Díaz, who spent over a year as a free agent before signing in 2025, scored his third goal in four games during a 5-2 victory against Osasuna on Sunday. He was upstaged by Lucas Boyé, whose hat-trick included an absolute belter from 35 yards out. “I didn’t even think about it,” the Argentinian striker said.

View image in fullscreen Lucas Boyé (left) wheels away after scoring Alavés’ third goal – his second of a hat-trick in a 5-2 win over Osasuna. Photograph: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images

One Argentina striker who is having considerably less fun is Julián Álvarez. Atlético were 2-0 down at Athletic Bilbao on Saturday by the time he entered the field to whistles from the travelling supporters. Nico Williams and Robert Navarro scored two in three minutes after the restart and Oihan Sancet added a late third. Diego Simeone opted not to comment on Álvarez not doing his post-match warm-down with the other substitutes.

Sports.title: Serie A’s hierarchy takes shape with wild night in Milan and flat draw in Turin | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Already as the words were being spoken, Cristian Chivu started to bristle. “Scontri diretti” translates to “head-to-head clashes”. The term is commonly deployed in a football context as a shorthand for those high-stakes games between teams who are expected to finish close together in the table – much like “six-pointers” in the English game.

Chivu’s Inter finished 11 points clear atop Serie A last season, his first as their head coach, but caught criticism along the way for an early Champions League exit and underperformance in some scontri diretti. Inter lost four out of six games against Napoli, Milan and Juventus. Their only win, at home to the Bianconeri, came after Alessandro Bastoni deceived a referee to get Pierre Kalulu sent off.

But did the media mis-sell the importance of these fixtures? Nobody could doubt they were big occasions. Napoli were defending champions at the time, Inter share one of world football’s most iconic stadiums, San Siro, with Milan, and their rivalry with Juventus has earned its nickname as the Derby d’Italia.

Of those clubs, however, only Napoli truly challenged Inter for the title. Even then, not that fiercely. Milan and Juventus finished fifth and sixth respectively. Inter won all their games against Roma and Como, who took third and fourth. Suffice to say, Chivu has not forgotten these details.

View image in fullscreen Massimiliano Allegri and Cristian Chivu are friendly before the scontri diretti. Photograph: Marco Alpozzi/LaPresse/AP

“Oh, I have missed this!” he cut in when a journalist broached the topic at a press conference leading up to Saturday’s home game against Napoli. “What are the scontri diretti? Which ones are they? The games against teams who finish in the top four? Or the ones all about tradition? Milan and Juve last season, where should we put them? They finished a long way behind. Are they not scontri diretti any more?”

He would later insist that this had not been a jab at any club, and that he personally considered every game a scontro diretto, even if facing the team in last place. Still, what a timely moment to remind everyone of Juventus and Milan’s recently diminished status, with those clubs facing off in Turin on Sunday night.

Seasons are not defined in early September, but these were fascinating early tests of all four teams’ progress. The newspaper Il Corriere dello Sport billed Inter-Napoli on its front page as “The New Classico”, a rivalry that has grown increasingly fascinating as the two clubs have dominated Serie A in the 2020s. They have won five of the past six Scudetti between them and even shared a head coach, Antonio Conte, during this decade.

Now Napoli are led by Massimiliano Allegri, formerly of Milan and Juventus; a man whose stale tactics in a home defeat by Como saw him portrayed as a dinosaur, but who steered his new team into a two-goal lead at Inter on Saturday.

The first half was goalless but not without incident. Within six minutes of kick-off, both keepers were forced into full-length stops. Federico Dimarco hit the post for Inter before the interval.

It was after the break, though, that magnificent chaos took hold. Inter appealed for a handball penalty, then Matteo Politano opened the scoring at the other end – driving home at the second attempt to punish some panicked defending. Rasmus Højlund made it 2-0 to the visitors in the 53rd minute. Lautaro Martínez pulled one back for Inter in the 56th.

Riveting, rapturous madness. Inter with the defiance of champions, and Napoli sending on Kevin De Bruyne and David Neres to chase a third goal instead of sitting on their lead. Marcus Thuram struck woodwork for the Nerazzurri then equalised in the 82nd minute. A dagger for Allegri, who had resisted his more cautious instincts right up to the 80th, when he finally sent on Benoît Badiashile as a third central defender.

And still that was not the end of it. Napoli blew two more golden opportunities to win. Neres made all the wrong choices after De Bruyne put him through. Frank Anguissa missed an open goal from two yards.

Then, as the 90th minute elapsed, Inter’s new signing Curtis Jones – the Englishman making his first home appearance off the bench after joining from Liverpool – swung a ball into the box. After a scramble, it broke to Lautaro, who jabbed home before scaling the partition that separates fans from the pitch behind the goal. Inter victorious in the scontro diretto, 3-2.

Sunday night’s game did not deliver the same level of entertainment. There has not been a single goalless draw so far in this Serie A season but with more than an hour played at the Allianz Stadium, it appeared that Juventus-Milan would be the first. Four of their past five Serie A meetings had ended goalless, and for all the talk of new chapters on both sides, this game felt like more of the same.

A hard reality check, for both sets of fans, after seeing their teams start the campaign with two wins. Juventus and Milan each spent more than €160m on transfers this summer, but few of their arrivals shone. Randal Kolo Muani and Gonçalo Ramos, salvaged at vast expense from Paris Saint-Germain’s pile of spare parts, started up front for either side, and managed one shot between them, which was off target.

Juventus at least had willing runners in Francisco Conceição, Nico González and Kerim Alajbegovic. The former tested Mike Maignan early and struck a post later on. Milan’s head coach, Ruben Amorim, dropped two of his best attacking performers so far this season, giving €50m signing Diego Moreira his first start ahead of Samuel Chukwueze at right wing-back and pairing Adrien Rabiot with Alexis Saelemaekers behind the attack at the expense of Alphadjo Cisse.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Milan were almost completely without threat. They finished the game on 0.10 expected goals. About half of that came from a shot by Cisse, assisted by Chukwueze, after both players entered as second-half substitutes. Somehow, it wound up in the net.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Serie A results Genoa 1-4 Como, Fiorentina 1-2 Torino, Inter 3-2 Napoli, Roma 2-1 Atalanta, Frosinone 3-2 Venezia, Parma 1-1 Monza, Bologna 2-2 Sassuolo, Juventus 1-1 Milan Monday: Cagliari v Lecce, Udinese v Lazio Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

A testament to teenager Cisse’s audacity and precision. He stepped away from Manuel Locatelli and nutmegged Pierre Kalulu to find the corner from an inauspicious angle. It was a second goal in three games for the breakout talent, who played on loan last season with Catanzaro in Serie B.

Milan were on course for a scandalous smash and grab, but Juventus threw everything they had on from the bench. In the end it was not the newly acquired Nick Woltemade, but instead a repurposed centre-back, Federico Gatti, who got on the end of Teun Koopmeiners’s cross to rescue a 1-1 draw.

View image in fullscreen Federico Gatti was the unexpected goalscorer for Juventus. Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/Reuters

It is not the first time he has dug Juventus out of a hole. After scoring a 93rd-minute equaliser against Roma this March, Gatti noted that he used to play in midfield when he was younger. He joked at the time that he could bag “15-20 goals a season” if they let him play up front. Instead, Juventus tried unsuccessfully to sell him over the summer. “I’m sorry you’re surprised,” he told an interviewer who remarked on his being the goalscoring hero once again. “My past says this is who I am, I have a force inside me that never dies.”

He had earned the right to chide his doubters. Still, there was something in the contrast between his wobbly steward-assisted climb on to an advertising hoarding with that image of Lautaro bounding over the hoardings to scale the partition at San Siro one night before.

The season is barely begun, and the Nerazzurri showed plenty of their own vulnerabilities this weekend. But these two early scontri diretti – if we may call them that – reinforced the impression that both Juventus and Milan have a way to travel before they can dream of title challenges yet.

Sports.title: Kim Milton Nielsen’s 1998 memories: ‘Hey, you are the man who sent off Beckham’
Sports.content:
At half-time on 30 June 1998, Kim Milton Nielsen stepped into the changing room at the Geoffroy-Guichard Stadium in Saint-Étienne. The air reeked of wet towels. He hugged his assistants. They’d just taken charge of the best half of football they’d ever officiated.

Argentina v England. World Cup round of 16. Michael Owen had terrorised Argentina with blistering runs and his breakout goal. A clever free-kick had outsmarted the English defence. Nielsen had awarded two penalties. He couldn’t wait for the second half, but he didn’t know what was coming.

View image in fullscreen England’s David Batty takes the ball away from Argentina’s Sergio Berti as Nielsen watches on. Photograph: Bob Thomas/Getty Images

At 37, Nielsen was refereeing his first major international tournament. He’d been trusted with the showcase match. Tensions between Argentina and England had simmered since the 1982 Falklands war, and deepened through controversial World Cup ​clashes – Geoff Hurst’s goal in 1966; Diego Maradona’s handball 20 years later. A loss for either side would be colossal.

And then it happened.

Diego Simeone clattered into David Beckham. Nielsen blew his whistle to book Simeone. Simeone leaned on Beckham and tugged his hair. Beckham flicked his boot; Simeone fell. Nielsen blew again. Red card for Beckham.

View image in fullscreen David Beckham aims his now infamous kick at Diego Simeone in England’s 1998 World Cup defeat. Photograph: BBC Sport

But it wasn’t going to be that easy. Sending off Beckham, a global superstar, at a World Cup with a full half still to play. A voice in Nielsen’s head whispered: was it really violent? Didn’t Simeone provoke it? Then he recognised the voice. He’d heard it before. It had nearly beaten him. He knew what to do.

Nielsen’s mind flicked back to 1991, when he was in his early 30s, refereeing Barcelona at the Camp Nou. A Sparta Prague player broke through on goal and was cynically fouled by Guillermo Amor. Before 82,000 Barça fans, he needed to send off one of their heroes. His instincts urged leniency – a free-kick and a yellow.

“Barcelona at home against a team from eastern Europe … it would be very easy to close your eyes and not do anything,” Nielsen told me. But he dug deep. Red card.

Sparta Prague scored from the free-kick. Nielsen’s heart sank. “I thought: ‘Oh my God, I am going to die at the Nou Camp.’” But the press admired the decision. It was a vital lesson. Whether it’s a big team or a small team, a superstar or a debutant, the same rules apply. Now, standing there, in front of Beckham, Nielsen reminded himself of that lesson.

That night, after England’s loss on penalties, Nielsen wondered if there was more he could have done. Then he realised something important. “If I changed my mind because I was afraid of the headlines, I would have destroyed myself as a referee,” he said. The cost of fairness is high. Sometimes referees must pay.

View image in fullscreen Referee Kim Milton Nielsen will always be remembered as the man who sent off David Beckham against Argentina. Photograph: Adam Butler/PA

Being called up for a World Cup was a highlight of Nielsen’s career, one that started in Copenhagen in 1976. He retired in 2006, but remains one of football’s iconic officials. In February 2005, he became the first referee to reach 50 appearances in the Champions League. But he’ll always be remembered as the man who sent off David Beckham. “I am surprised, and I have been surprised since, because even small boys who were not born in 1998, they come up to me and they say, ‘Hey, you are the man who sent off David Beckham,’” Nielsen told me.

And he is quietly proud of it.

This is an extract from The Impossible Job: The Truly Unbelievable World of a Football Referee by William Ralston (Viking, £22). To support the Guardian, order your copy at guardianbookshop.com. Delivery charges may apply

Sports.title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw
Sports.content:
David Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind to salvage a point against Manchester United through Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.

The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.

Tyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.

The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.

“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.

“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”

Moyes also paid tribute to the quality of the goals from Maitland-Niles and George, who cancelled out finishes from Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko respectively.

“If nobody knew you that goal would get you plenty of headlines,” he said of Maitland-Niles, a £4.3m deadline-day signing from Lyon. “It was a brilliant goal, brilliant technique. We have not had a chance to get to know Ainsley but it was a great start from him.”

Sports.title: Impressive Anthony Gordon matches Lionel Messi record for Barcelona and tipped for surprise role
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon has been tipped to play as a striker for Barcelona after he impressed by equalling a Lionel Messi record.

The England winger continued his strong start to life in Spain on Sunday, as he provided an assist in Barca's 5-0 victory over Valencia.

4 Anthony Gordon has made history with his stunning assist record in LaLiga so far Credit: AFP

After his £70million arrival from Barcelona, Gordon has hit the ground running in LaLiga.

Despite being yet to score, the 25-year-old took his assist tally to five in his first four league outings against Valencia.

He kept up his stunning record by teeing up Fermin Lopez in the 22nd minute - received the ball in the area with his back from goal before laying it off to the Spaniard to smash home.

Gordon joins exclusive club

Gordon has now joined an exclusive club by becoming one of just four players to record assists in their first four matches of a LaLiga season.

And the Englishman is among illustrious company here, with Lionel Messi among the stars to previously record the impressive feat.

Messi - who recently announced his retirement from Argentina duty - also provided five assists at the start of the 2011/12 campaign.

Gordon will certainly be hoping to emulate the football megastar's historic campaign in other ways too, with Messi famously recording an historic 91-goal calendar year across the 2011/12 campaign.

Real Madrid icons Juanito (1980/81) and Michel (1987/88) are among the other two stars to notch the impressive assist numbers, with the former teeing up seven goals and the latter laying on a staggering seven in their respective campaigns.

Central role?

Gordon's fast start to life at Barcelona has led talkSPORT's Kevin Hatchard to tip him to fill in at centre forward with the Spanish giants lacking a focal point up front after summer departures.

Robert Lewandowski's departure for Chicago Fire saw Barca lose their main source of goals, before Ferran Torres left to join PSG.

4 There is a lack of recognised goalscorer at Barcelona following Robert Lewandowski's summer exit Credit: Getty

4 Gordon's fellow attackers Lamine Yamal and Raphinha both got on the scoresheet in the Valencia rout Credit: Getty

Meanwhile Marcus Rashford ultimately saw a permanent move to Catalonia fall through, with the Manchester United forward capable of playing across the forward line.

So far this season, Hansi Flick's side have played a fluid front three of Gordon, Raphinha and Lamine Yamal, with Raphinha the more central player.

While Gabriel Jesus' arrival from Arsenal provides a centre forward option, Hatchard believes we could well see Gordon deployed here.

Discussing Gordon on talkSPORT's Trans Euro Express, Hatchard said: “I've been really impressed with the way he's slotted into this team."

He continued: “You're talking about the lack of a number nine per se, with Torres and Lewandowski moving on.

"I know Gabriel Jesus has gone in there, but he's quite versatile as well.

4 Gordon's has been tipped to showcase his versatility at Barcelona, having done so before at Newcastle Credit: Getty

“And I think Gordon's going to play some minutes through the middle. I think he looks really, really comfortable on and off the pitch and I think that helps.“

Gordon already has experience of playing centrally, having deputised in the role for Newcastle last season amid a goalscoring crisis.

Overall, the England star scored nine goals in 16 starts in the position last term, netting five times in his three starts in the role.

That includes a goal against Barcelona in the Champions League league phase last September, and a four-goal haul in Newcastle's round of 16 play-off first leg against Qarabag.

Sports.title: Supercomputer makes huge Arsenal Champions League prediction as two surprise teams ahead of PSG
Sports.content:
Opta's supercomputer has spoken, and it's good news for Arsenal fans.

The Gunners go into this season's Champions League campaign hoping to go one better, having fallen agonisingly short against Paris Saint-Germain last term.

3 Arsenal have lost all four of their major European finals, dating back to 2000 Credit: Getty

Gabriel's skied penalty during the shootout handed PSG a second-straight European crown and ensured further heartbreak for Arsenal in continental action.

However, Opta has predicted that this season is when Arsenal's wait for a major European trophy will end.

Opta predicts Arsenal's Champions League chances

Their supercomputer has given the Gunners a 21.2 per cent chance of winning the Champions League.

Mikel Arteta's side established themselves as a dominant force in European action last term as they became the first team to win all eight fixtures during the league phase of the competition.

However, that will be difficult to replicate as the Gunners lost attacking trio Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard in the summer.

Christos Tzolis, a left-winger, was the only addition to Arsenal's attacking stocks, meaning Arteta will have to get crafty with his selections if he is to keep his squad fresh and compete on multiple fronts.

Of course, Arsenal can replenish their squad in the January window to give themselves a much-needed boost in their quest for a maiden Champions League crown.

Simon Jordan's verdict on why Arsenal need a Champions League title

Victory in the Champions League is something Simon Jordan needs to see in order for the Gunners to truly rubber-stamp their era of dominance.

"Let's see what they do in Europe," Jordan said on Monday's edition of White and Jordan.

"They have a chance to win the Premier League. A lot of other teams are in flux. They might have gone and spent money like you've never seen, but they're still in flux. There are still teams changing from legacy managers to change directions at other football clubs that are trying to reboot themselves, so that gives Arsenal a head start in retaining the Premier League.

3 Arteta is aiming to do what Wenger couldn't and lead Arsenal to European glory Credit: Getty

"But when we start talking about a football club that's dominant, at the top of its game and really owning its space, let them do it in Europe too, because PSG do it."

However, former Arsenal Premier League title winner Emmanuel Petit felt Arteta leading the Gunners to string together consecutive domestic crowns should not be overlooked.

"From what I've seen in the last few weeks, I think the confidence and quality, they (Arsenal) have," Petit said on White and Jordan.

"I think Arsenal, if they can go back-to-back in the Premier League, that would be a huge achievement.

"Champions League is really important, but I think they are among the teams this season that can win it."

Who are the other Champions League contenders predicted by Opta?

As for the other contenders, Opta has tipped Bayern Munich as Arsenal's biggest threat for the title, with the Germans given a 19.9 per cent chance of winning.

3 Bayern's European hopes will likely rest on Harry Kane's shoulders Credit: Getty

Vincent Kompany's side made it to the semi-finals last season but were beaten by eventual champions PSG, who prevailed 6-5 on aggregate.

Should Opta's predictions ring true, fans could be treated to a preview of what's to come when Bayern host Arsenal in a league phase fixture on October 21.

With Arsenal and Bayern cemented as the two favourites, attention turns to who is the third-leading contender.

According to Opta's supercomputer, that would be Manchester City, who have a 12 per cent chance of winning.

It would be an almighty feat for City, who won the Champions League for the first time in the 2022/23 campaign.

However, in the seasons that have followed since, City have only gone as far as the quarter-final, and that stage has been reached just once, meaning new boss Enzo Maresca has his work cut out for him in continental action.

Surprisingly, defending champions PSG are fourth favourites with a 7.7. per cent chance.

The Parisians are gunning for a hat-trick of Champions League titles, something which has only been accomplished by Real Madrid (15/16, 16/17, 17/18).

Sports.title: Man United told to expect ‘some beatings’ in Champions League as Gary Neville outlines major concerns
Sports.content:
Gary Neville highlighted worrying errors from Patrick Dorgu, Andrey Santos and Leny Yoro led to Manchester United conceding late at Everton.

Major concerns were raised about United's defensive issues, with Gabby Agbonlahor warning they will get found out in the Champions League.



3 Maitland-Niles ensured United missed out on victory by scoring a late screamer Credit: Getty

Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored an outstanding equaliser in stoppage time on his Everton debut to seal a 2-2 draw on Sunday.

United thought they wrapped up three points in the 88th minute as Benjamin Sesko headed in from a Luke Shaw cross.

However, the long-range effort from Maitland-Niles flew past Senne Lammens and into the top corner to ensure the points were shared.



The result has left United with just one win from three in the Premier League this season, and club legend Neville highlighted the defensive fragilities from three players that led to the crushing blow.

"Manchester United are conceding two goals a game," he explained on his podcast. "From a United perspective, you can't concede two goals a game, they're on track to concede 76 goals if they carry on.



"They won't concede 76 goals, but the thing that I think needed to happen beyond the transfer window, with the questions that have been asked about the defence was that Manchester United, one, needed to win today. But secondly, they couldn't concede goals.

"There may be some people that lazily could say, 'They were two spectacular goals'. I mean, that last goal is a really bad one. It's a really bad one because they're on that far side, you know you've got Jack Grealish down on the left...



"Dorgu, for some reason, chases out and presses, isolated press. Santos then doesn't go over behind him and stays back, and it just gets played past Dorgu. It's a massive mistake, that.

"It's a massive mistake from Dorgu, but he might have been told to go and press by Santos. I don't believe he will have done, it just strikes me with a lot of lack of communication.

"(Diogo) Dalot went off, and Yoro comes on at right-back. He's narrow and tucked in, and deep, as are the other back four players, and (Noussair) Mazraoui is at left-back, so United have had to change their back four again during the match.

3 Neville has explained the defensive mess that led to the goal Credit: Getty



"Yoro coming in at right-back, I'm sorry, that for me highlights the problem, because he plays so narrow. If you look at what happens on that last goal, forget the last bit, the keeper can't do anything about it, it's a special strike.

"A lot happens before that goal goes in the back of Manchester United's net. When you're playing against a team, it's 2-1, you're away at Everton, at Hill Dickinson Stadium, you've got to push up, you've got to make sure that you don't get players sprinting off and doing stupid things.

"Dorgu sprints forward, the ball gets played past him, and Everton just drift down that left-hand side so easily. Santos doesn't get across, and then when Santos doesn't get across quickly enough.

"Yoro is deep and narrow, almost playing like a third/fourth narrow centre-back, waiting for the ball to go into the box.



"They could have stopped it at source, so that to me is a real error in the lead-up to that.

"I was screaming as it happened, because you know full well you're going to get the ball pumped into your box or you're going to get a shot against you, or you're going to get a team being desperate in the last few minutes.

3 United have been tipped for more defensive frailties in the Champions League Credit: Getty

"So you have to make sure that you're organised, and United weren't organised in that last couple of minutes, and teams think they've got a chance against them."



United set for Champions League 'beatings'

Neville is not the only one concerned with the United back four, as Gabby Agbonlahor has also raised questions over their quality.

The talkSPORT pundit has even predicted them to suffer some heavy losses in the Champions League this season, with United beginning their league phase campaign against Sabah FK on Thursday night.

"Harry Maguire, I thought he had a good game," Agbonlahor said: "I look at Lisandro Martinez, I'm not sold on him, I think he can be the weak link, especially when crosses come in.

"Luke Shaw, very good going forward, maybe not as good defensively yesterday. And Dalot, when Jack Grealish came on, he was giving away fouls, he had to get taken off for Yoro, who came in on that right-hand side.



"Yoro, big-money signing, he should be starting, he should be saying to himself, 'I should be starting in this side.'"

"I think they're going to get some beatings in the Champions League," he added. "With that back four, and the quality in the Champions League, they're going to get found out."

Sports.title: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid LIVE commentary: Diego Simeone set for hostile Anfield return
Sports.content:
Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home to Atletico Madrid this week.

3 Atletico are looking to win at Anfield in 90 minutes for the first time Credit: Getty

However, the result was overshadowed by unsavoury scenes involving Atletico boss Diego Simeone.

The Argentine coach had to be held back by security as he clashed with Reds supporters following the winning goal.

Simeone can likely expect another hostile reception as he takes to the dugout this week.



Liverpool have won their last three meetings with Atletico, dating back to a defeat in March 2020.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi told to make two instant changes to fix Tottenham’s goalscoring drought
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi told to make two instant changes to fix Tottenham’s goalscoring drought

Roberto De Zerbi has been urged to start James Maddison and Dominic Solanke to fix Tottenham’s goalscoring drought.

Spurs' poor start to the season continued on Saturday, as they were held to a 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest which saw them remain goalless in the Premier League.

6 Omar Marmoush is yet to register a goal involvement for Spurs

With three games played, Spurs have not scored a single league goal this season and sit 17th in the table after two defeats and a draw.

This saw De Zerbi's side fall to an unwanted 52-year first, having last failed to find the back of the net in their opening three league games in the 1974/75 season.

It marks a worrying start to the campaign for the north Londoners, who again looked void of attacking quality despite their huge summer spending.

After narrowly avoiding relegation last term, Spurs splashed out over £300million on new recruits in a bid to become competitive again.

This includes the arrivals of attacking duo Savio and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City for a total sum of £145m.

However, the pair - forming a fluid front three alongside Mathys Tel - were unable to inspire any real goal threat against Forest, with Spurs failing to manage a shot on target in the clash.

Agbonlahor calls for changes

Tottenham's lack of goalscoring threat has led talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor to call for Solanke and Maddison to return to Spurs' starting line-up to provide an attacking focal point and creativity.

Agbonlahor insisted it is no shock Spurs' summer signings are struggling, pointing to Savio and Marmoush's struggles at Man City.

Asked if Spurs had shown any sign of improvement, he told talkSPORT Breakfast: “No. Are you surprised, though?

"Savio - 31 appearances in the Premier League and Champions League last season, one goal, two assists.

6 Despite scoring on his Spurs debut in the Carabao Cup, Savio has been unable to have the same impact in the Premier League Credit: Getty

6 Mykhailo Mudryk struggled to make an impact off the bench against Forest following his deadline day switch from Chelsea Credit: Getty

“Marmoush - three goals in 29 appearances in the Premier League and Champions League last season.

“Don't get me started on Tel, after that free kick a couple of weeks ago [against Newcastle].

“They haven't got the quality. It's alright spending this big money on Manchester City rejects who aren't goalscorers. What do you expect?

"Solanke has to start in the game.”

Agbonlahor continued: “They need Maddison back in there. They need Solanke leading the line, and then two wingers off them.

“But it's a big worry to not score yet.”

6 Dominic Solanke scored in Spurs' 5-1 Carabao Cup thrashing of Charlton - the only game they have scored in this term Credit: Getty

6 James Maddison missed Spurs' draw with Nottingham Forest with a shoulder injury Credit: Getty

De Zerbi urges calm

Despite growing frustration among fans over his side's toothless start the campaign, De Zerbi has insisted his Tottenham side are a work in progress.

Speaking to talkSPORT after the Forest draw, he stressed Spurs are in the process of rebuilding, having overhauled the spine of the team.

As well as signing attacking players Savio, Marmoush and Mykhailo Mudryk, Spurs broke their transfer record twice, spending £185m combined on midfielders Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, and brought in defender Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton.

De Zerbi told talkSPORT's Geoff Peters: "I think we are working to build a different Tottenham than the last two seasons.

"And even (though) we made a great window of the transfer market, we need time.

"Because the football team becomes a football team with the time, with the relationship with the players, between the players, the connection between the players to find a balance because it's not so easy to find a balance with a lot of new players.

6 De Zerbi is remaining calm despite Spurs' winless run extending to three games Credit: AFP

"I'm excited to work with these players.

"And if you analyse the history of the Premier League in the last ten seasons, ten years, many big clubs, they wanted to rebuild the team.

"Sometimes they finish in a good way, sometimes not, but anyway, they spent the time to become top."

3 Millwall take on Newcastle this week for the first time in 33 years Credit: Getty
