Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star sacked from first manager job after just 98 days in charge
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star sacked from first manager job after just 98 days in charge

Glenn Whelan has been sacked by Livingston after just five league games in charge, with former boss David Martindale taking interim charge.

The ex-Stoke and Aston Villa midfielder was named head coach of the Scottish outfit in May in his first managerial role.

3 Glenn Whelan's first permanent head coach job lasted just over three months Credit: Getty

However, Whelan endured a challenging start to life in the dugout and things took a turn for the worse on Friday.

His Livingston side failed to qualify for the knockout rounds of the Premier Sports Cup after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Stenhousemuir - managed by his predecessor Marvin Bartley.

On top of a disappointing cup exit, Whelan picked up just six points from his first five league matches in Scotland.

Livi have won two and lost three - including each of their last two against semi-professional sides Arbroath and Stenhousemuir.

And this proved to be the final straw for Whelan, as it was announced on Sunday night that he would not be continuing in his role.

Livingston statement

In a club statement on Sunday night, Livingston chairman Calvin Ford confirmed that Whelan and his assistant Danny Ventre would be leaving the West Lothian outfit.

Sporting director Martindale will return to the dugout to take interim charge - having previously managed the club from 2020 until February of this year - alongside Frankie McAvoy

Ford wrote: “After careful consideration and thorough discussions, the Club can confirm that head coach Glenn Whelan and assistant head coach Danny Ventre are no longer with the organisation.

“On behalf of everyone at Livingston, I want to express our gratitude for their hard work, dedication and service during their time with us.

“In the short term, David Martindale & Frankie McAvoy will temporarily step in as interim coaches assisted by Grant Murray and Brian Potter.

3 Whelan is best known for making over 300 Premier League appearances for Stoke

“Davie’s past success and proven track record in the Scottish Championship made this decision easy and we look forward to refocusing and finding success on the pitch while he holds this position.

“Looking ahead, we have already begun the process of securing the appropriate search firm to help us find our next head coach.

“Our net will be cast far wider than it was in our previous search and the focus of the search will be via data analytics that fit in with the clubs game model and other important criteria that will aid Livingston in finding the ideal candidate to lead our club forward."

Livingston finished rock bottom of the Scottish Premiership - 13 points adrift of closest rivals St Mirren - winning just two games all season.

And the club pointed to their desire to secure an immediate top-flight return as part of their decision to seek a new manager.

The statement continued: "Mediocrity is not an acceptable solution, and we will continue to work to find the leader that delivers on the ambitions and aspirations of sustained, high-level success that we expect at Livingston.

3 Whelan lasted just four months at Livingston, having previously had interim stints at Wigan and Bristol Rovers Credit: Getty

"Nothing else is acceptable. As always, we are led by the credo that the club comes first.

"We are driven by our desire to win and compete at the highest level, and we feel that this decision is appropriate given the unfortunate start to the 2026/27 season."

Glenn Whelan's managerial career

Whelan's sacking by Livingston marks the end of a tough first permanent role in senior management.

The ex-midfielder - who made over 250 Premier League appearances for Stoke - had previous coaching experience at Bristol Rovers and Wigan.

He had two brief spells as interim manager of the latter, stepping in after Shaun Maloney and Ryan Lowe's respective sackings.

On top of this, Whelan has also worked in the Ireland coaching set-up when John O'Shea took temporary charge in 2024, and spent time as part of Ireland’s youth international programme at Under-16 level before this.

Sports.title: Krystian Bielik ‘should be banned for entire season’ for throat grab as ex-teammate offers brutal verdict
Sports.content:
Krystian Bielik ‘should be banned for entire season’ for throat grab as ex-teammate offers brutal verdict

Krystian Bielik should be handed a season-long ban for appearing to grab a young Portsmouth fan by the neck.

That's the view of talkSPORT presenter Sam Matterface as the Cardiff City defender faces a sanction from the Football Association (FA).

3 Bielik is facing FA action for an incident involving a Portsmouth fan

Footage appears to show Bielik grabbing a Portsmouth supporter's neck during their Championship fixture on Saturday afternoon.

The incident at Fratton Park occurred when the Cardiff man, on loan from West Brom, attempted to retrieve the ball from the crowd.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy claimed that Bielik had been slapped in the face during the altercation, with Portsmouth manager John Mousinho apologising for what happened.

talkSPORT understands that the FA are 'aware' of the incident and have been awaiting the match report from referee Ben Speedie.

Hampshire Police are also investigating, and Matterface believes that Bielik should be suspended for the rest of the 2026/27 season.

Bielik should be 'banned for the season'

"He's going to get a hefty ban, and rightly so," talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said on Premier League All Access.

"I don't think he should play again this season," Matterface replied, to which former Premier League striker Troy Deeney added: "I played with him at Birmingham City and trust me, if that kid would have just farted near him, he would have s*** himself.

"I cannot believe that you could grab a fan. Trust me, in my day, I've wanted to. I've had people do all sorts and say all sorts. You can't grab a fan."

"All this lad did was chuck the ball over his head," Crook insisted. "He made him look a fool, nothing more. There was nothing malicious about what the kid did."

Deeney explained: "I think he should be reprimanded the right way. For the first time ever, I'd actually ask for FA Sam to get involved, because he'd make sure this was done properly."

3 Matterface has called for Bielik to miss the rest of the season Credit: Getty

"Yeah, I would," Matterface responded. "I wouldn't let him play again this season, because I think there are certain rules.

"I think there are rules about fans not engaging with the players, I don't think that can happen. Or managers, everyone's safety on the pitch has to be paramount.

"But similarly, you have to make sure that it works the other way as well. Especially if you're talking about a child.

"Now, I don't know how old the kid was... but the fact of the matter is, is that he's thrown the ball over his head, he's having a bit of a laugh and a joke.

"It's banter, it's football banter. My word, that happens up and down the country every single week. I mean, get over yourself.

"To grab anyone around the neck is absolutely outrageous. To grab a child in that manner borders on criminal, actually."

3 Police are also investigating the incident Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"As someone who knows the criminal justice system, it actually is criminal," Deeney confirmed.

Matterface then concluded: "I wonder what will happen to him but, for me, that's it, he shouldn't play again this season."

Portsmouth won the match 2-0 and sit 14th in the Championship, whilst Cardiff are winless in 22nd.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's boring act is an art, combustible Roberto De Zerbi may not stay long at Spurs - and the TNT pundit who is never insightful enough: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend
Sports.content:
If Manchester United had a defence as reliable and immovable as the one their manager presents to the world, then they would be higher up the Premier League table.

Michael Carrick is proving himself spectacularly impossible to penetrate – whether his team win, lose or draw – and it’s exactly what his team and his club need at this stage of their evolution.

Carrick is not a dull man but he is making an art form of coming across as such. In doing so, he is making sure that he doesn’t add any of the unhelpful noise that always surrounds English football’s best-supported and most newsworthy football club.

One of the challenges facing anybody managing the modern United is that the club exists in an almost constant boom and bust cycle in terms of its publicity.

If United win, they are back for good. If they don’t, they are useless. A section of the fanbase buys into it, social media accelerates and inflames it while the mainstream Press also plays its part.

When you then throw in the host of ex-United players speaking on weekly podcasts and working on TV then the picture is clear. Other big clubs feel a bit of this too. But nobody feels it quite like United do.

So when a manager such as Ruben Amorim, Erik ten Hag or the never-to-be-forgotten Ralf Rangnick add their own soundbites to the cacophony then United are sure to occupy more media space than can ever be healthy at a time when the club is almost a decade and a half into its search for post-Sir Alex Ferguson stability.

There is a clear sense that Carrick knows and understands this. He has a 15-year connection with the club as player and manager after all. His policy to be as boring as is humanly possible feels deliberate.

One of the challenges facing anybody managing the modern United is that the club exists in a near constant boom and bust cycle in terms of publicity, and Carrick is searching for stability

After Carrick suggested his players had made some poor decisions in the game at Everton, he seemed to sense he had said – by his standards – far too much and quickly backed down

Indeed he is the first manager since Ferguson who appears to have a clear media strategy. With the likes of the three mentioned above and men such as Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho and David Moyes, it sometimes felt possible to stare straight into their soul. Try that with Carrick and you only see cardboard staring back.

Listening to him speak to reporters and TV and radio crews after his team’s wobbly 2-2 draw at Everton was to sense only a little frustration at the result.

When it was put to him by the BBC that it must have been painful to concede such a late goal, Carrick’s reply lasted six words.

‘Yeah, yeah for sure it is,’ he said.

After he suggested his players had made some poor decisions in the game, he seemed to sense he had said – by his standards – far too much.

Asked to elaborate, he said: ‘I will keep that to myself.’

Everton need to bring the noise

One thing that Carrick did say on Sunday was that Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium is a ‘tough place to play’ and he was actually wrong about that.

On the whole Everton’s new home is proving far too hospitable to visiting teams. Since Everton moved down to the water from Goodison Park at the start of last season, David Moyes’ team have won just seven of their 21 home games in Premier League.

The Hill Dickinson is a fabulous stadium to visit. Now that the infrastructure around it is starting to develop, it will undoubtedly be one of the very best stadiums in the country by the time the European Championship is played here in the summer of 2028.

But whether it serves Everton on the field at the moment is another matter. It is not remotely intimidating and only sprang to life on Sunday when Everton finally got on the front foot in the final half an hour.

Should a team inspire a crowd or a crowd inspire a team? Where does the responsibility lie? It’s an old question.

Go to a place like Elland Road in Leeds or St James’ Park in Newcastle and that dilemma feels irrelevant. It’s just noisy. It’s just hostile.

Everton and their supporters need to find a way to get to that place and to that sweet spot. Otherwise, opposing teams are going to continue approaching a trip to HDS like a nice day out by the Mersey.

The stadium only sprang to life on Sunday when Everton finally got on the front foot in the final half an hour

De Zerbi's stay could be short

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi is cut from different cloth than someone like Carrick. His post-match criticism of his players after a third game without a goal against Nottingham Forest was totally in keeping with character.

Criticising players by name as De Zerbi did with Omar Marmoush and Mathys Tel after his team’s 0-0 draw on Saturday is always risky but this is the coach Tottenham have hired.

The Italian did what was asked of him by making sure Spurs stayed up last season and is a very talented manager. But this was always unlikely to be a quiet stewardship.

De Zerbi is ambitious, aggressive and combustible. He says what he feels – both privately and publicly – and this is also very much his style when it comes to managing up to chief executives and sporting directors.

The 47-year-old has been a coach for 13 years and Tottenham is his ninth club. He signed a five-year deal last April but it would be entirely out of character if he stays remotely that long.

They admired and appreciated De Zerbi during his two seasons at Brighton but at the same time were not exactly devastated when he left for Marseille.

De Zerbi signed a five-year deal at Tottenham last April but it would be entirely out of character if he stays remotely that long

Glasner must beware the sharp knives

Winless Forest have nevertheless shown some positive signs under new coach Oliver Glasner and Neco Williams’ goal on Saturday should have stood. There was no conclusive VAR evidence that he had handled the ball as he bundled it in.

Glasner must beware the perils of the job, however.

Not only can owner Evangelos Marinakis be hard to handle, one Forest manager of last season has recently been grumbling about being stitched up by two members of his own dressing room.

He believes two players approached Marinakis to complain about his coaching shortly before he was sacked. And one of them still plays for the club.

Serie A is a step down

Still with Forest, it was a shame to see the talented Omari Hutchinson leave the club on loan to AC Milan.

The former Chelsea player was a star for Ipswich in their last Premier League season two years ago and was expected to shine when he moved to the City Ground a year ago.

Sadly, the 22-year-old has now joined the growing band of Premier League players farmed out to Serie A. People can dress it up whichever way they like but if you move to Italy these days it’s either because you are getting old or haven’t quite made the grade in England.

Omari Hutchinson has now joined the growing band of Premier League players farmed out to Serie A

One goal and out

If there was further evidence needed of just how unforgiving the English top-flight can be, then look no further than the case of Liam Millar.

The Canadian has been one of Hull’s early season heroes, scoring his team’s only goal in the win at Coventry nine days ago.

But by the time Sergej Jakirovic‘s team lined up for Saturday’s draw with Aston Villa, the 26-year-old had already been shipped out on loan to Birmingham.

Ouch.

Why isn't Glenn Hoddle a better pundit?

Match of the Day continues to evolve and added Rob Edwards and Ashley Young to its roster over the weekend. Both made solid debuts.

But what of TNT Sports?

Saturday’s offering from St James’ Park featured Joleon Lescott and Glenn Hoddle and was once again underwhelming. Hoddle, for some reason, is never quite the astute and insightful pundit that you would expect him to be.

TNT are in danger of falling too far behind standards set by Sky Sports.

Hoddle, for some reason, is never quite the astute and insightful pundit that you would expect him to be

Raya is top of my list

On the radio, 5 Live’s excellent Matthew Upson was gushing over David Raya’s distribution in the compelling Arsenal-Chelsea game.

The Spaniard – who is quite amazingly only third choice for Spain – is becoming the complete goalkeeper and is currently the best in the Premier League at a time when the likes of Liverpool’s Alisson Becker are now on the other side of the curve.

My Premier League top five goalkeepers are currently: David Raya, Emi Martinez, Jordan Pickford, Alisson, Senne Lammens.

Two other Englishmen – Dean Henderson at Crystal Palace and Leeds’ James Trafford – have also started the season well.

New rule fails Rogers

Perhaps the pick of this season’s new rules is that which says players must leave the field at the nearest point within ten seconds when substituted. It’s a decent weapon in the war on time wasting.

Morgan Rogers won’t be a fan though. After leaving the field at the Emirates on Sunday, the new Chelsea signing had to do a half lap of honour past fans of the club he chose not to join on leaving Aston Villa in the summer.

It didn’t go particularly well for him.

Enzo is well out of Chelsea muddle

Enzo Fernandez never looked like a £100million player while at Chelsea and the decision by Manchester City to take him off their hands for a whopping £125million seemed curious to say the least.

But the Argentina player’s debut for City – rather hurried after Nico O’Reilly’s late injury saw him promoted from the bench – was impressive. Not only did the 25-year-old set up Erling Haaland for City’s goal, he delivered another brilliantly imaginative pass for an effort that was subsequently ruled out for offside.

Maybe it was never Fernandez who was the problem at Chelsea but rather the environment in which he was asked to play. Another reason why we should view Xabi Alonso’s sound start at Stamford Bridge with a little caution.

Where are the right backs?

How hard can it really be for a top Premier League club to find a decent right-back?

Manchester City, for example, have never really found a top-class replacement for Kyle Walker.

New coach Enzo Maresca has the likes of Matheus Nunes and Rico Lewis to choose from but left both on the bench against Coventry, asking central defender Abdukodir Khusanov to play there.

Meanwhile at Liverpool, Andoni Iraola attempted to solve the same problem the same way at the start of the weekend.

Loan central defender Ronaldo Araujo was selected ahead of Jeremie Frimpong at Ipswich on Friday and though he was adequate enough, he certainly didn’t look like a long-term solution.

Manchester City have never really found a top-class replacement for Kyle Walker, with central defender Abdukodir Khusanov (above) asked to play at right back on the weekend

Ben is back... again

Ben Chilwell made an instant impact for his new club Crystal Palace, scoring the winner in a 3-2 ding-dong at Fulham.

I recall watching Chilwell form a fabulous left-sided partnership with Mason Mount as Thomas Tuchel’s Chelsea won the Champions League in 2021.

Since then, both have lost their way a little and Mount was an unused substitute for Manchester United on Sunday.

It may be too late for either to rekindle England ambitions. Chilwell, for example, will be 30 in December.

But having won a Premier League with Leicester, a Champions League with Chelsea and the FA Cup during his first spell at Palace, a very talented left back has an impressive medal haul for a guy who has been restricted by injury to a little more than 200 league appearances.

All bets are on

At a time when sport is endeavouring to preach caution regarding all things related to gambling, the line up of officials for Boreham Wood’s home game with Carlisle in the National League was unfortunate.

Referee Harry WAGER was assisted by linesman FIDLER and CONN.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Why Arsenal can dominate the Premier League for the rest of the decade - and the three very good reasons why they didn't need a top-class forward this summer
Sports.content:
Wesley Fofana knows all about what it’s like to try something unexpected, especially if it involves ducking down the hard shoulder of the A3 in his Lamborghini.

But not even multiple misadventures in his super car had prepared the Chelsea defender for the stunt that Kai Havertz pulled on him on Sunday afternoon at the Emirates.

There were a lot of beautiful moments of skill and drama in the Premier League this weekend and I’m thinking mainly of Cody Gakpo’s two assists for Liverpool against Ipswich, Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ equaliser for Everton against Manchester United and Josh King’s turn that bamboozled Chris Richards at Craven Cottage in the build-up to Fulham’s second goal against Crystal Palace.

But Havertz won the prize for his magic trick in north London. Christos Tzolis played the ball in to him on the edge of the Chelsea area and Havertz shaped to control it. At the last second, he ignored it instead and let it run into the path of Martin Odegaard.

Poor Fofana looked as if he had been hypnotised by the brilliance of it. While he was sleeping, Odegaard danced in and slammed the ball past Emi Martinez for Arsenal’s winner.

Chelsea will not be the last team to be left in a trance by Arsenal like that this season. It is very early in the campaign but Mikel Arteta’s team already looks like an upgrade on the side that just held off Manchester City to win the title for the first time in 22 years. Last season, wracked with tension, they crawled over the line. This season, their play is infused with joie de vivre.

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was in oustanding form at the Emirates on Sunday, producing one of the moments of the weekend with his delightful dummy against Chelsea

The piece of brilliance allowed Martin Odegaard to score the decisive second goal in a 2-1 win

They are going to be mighty hard to derail. And I don’t just mean this season. I mean for the rest of the decade. Now they have learned how to win, they look like a team that may just keep on winning.

Things can change quickly in football but this looks like the beginning of a dynasty at Arsenal. This looks like the beginning of a period of dominance, led by Arteta.

Perhaps that is disrespectful to Manchester City. They have not gone away. But there are too many variables with City. Will Enzo Maresca be an effective replacement for Pep Guardiola? Doubtful.

Will Enzo Fernandez get close to justifying the absurd £125million fee City paid for him? Highly doubtful. Will the weight of the 115 charges of financial impropriety ranged against the club start to take its toll? Will the judgment finally come this season? Will they be found innocent or guilty?

Arsenal do not face any of those complications. Maybe ‘serene’ is the wrong word to apply to a team that runs to the vibe of unadulterated intensity set by its manager but Arteta’s 2026-27 side looks smooth and assured. If its tone last season was set by the combativeness of Gabriel and the relentless excellence of Declan Rice, this season feels as if it may be defined by the nuance of Odegaard and Havertz.

That’s the other thing with this Arsenal side: some were underwhelmed by their dealings in the summer window, even if they bought proven, seasoned, top-class Premier League quality in Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes. And added Tzolis, too. But that’s only the half of it. Arsenal have acquired three other new players.

There were long periods last season when, because of injuries they were all dealing with, it felt as if Havertz, Odegaard and Bukayo Saka were not really there. In the crunch, much of the burden fell on Gabriel and William Saliba and David Raya and, particularly, Rice. But now the cavalry’s back.

Odegaard seems rejuvenated by the World Cup, where he starred in Norway’s exuberant run to the quarter-finals. He is playing like a dream this season. He is playing with elan and confidence and desire. His goal in the Community Shield, when he sat down Gianluigi Donnarumma with a delicious feint, was the first indication of the change that has come over him.

Havertz looks like a new player, too. When he joined Chelsea from Bayer Leverkusen in 2020, many German commentators described him as a ‘generational talent’. I’ve never quite seen that, even though he scored the winner for Chelsea against City in one Champions League final and added another for Arsenal in last season’s defeat in the final, on penalties, by Paris Saint-Germain.

Odegaard has been a player reborn this season and seems rejuvenated by the World Cup, where he starred in Norway’s run to the quarter-finals

It was rare last season for Arsenal to have Bukayo Saka (left), Havertz (second right) and Odegaard (right) on the pitch at the same time

But now I’m starting to see it. Havertz gives this Arsenal side an entirely different dimension to the way they looked when they were playing with Viktor Gyokeres as their spearhead last season. Gyokeres was a blunt force but Havertz brings style and guile and intelligence. If he can stay fit, he will make a huge difference to Arsenal’s season.

And Saka? Well, the importance of Saka does not need any explanation any more. He was also dogged by injury last season and he also looks like a player keen to make up for what he missed. The hunger he showed to score the winner at Villa Park last Monday night was a sign of that. Before the campaign started, he was my tip for Footballer of the Year. I don’t see any reason to amend that.

There will be slip-ups and there will be stumbles. There always are during the course of a season. But when they come, Arsenal will be even better equipped to deal with them. They look formidable. They look like a dynasty forming.

DYER DELIGHT AS SOUTHEND WIN A THRILLER

By the time Southend United played Yeovil Town at Roots Hall early on Saturday afternoon, footage of Southend boss Kieron Dyer squeezing as many Michael Jackson song titles as he could into the pre-match press conference for charity had gone viral. Bad, Thriller and Billie Jean all got mentions. I was worried he might have made himself a hostage to fortune when Southend went 2-0 down in their National League fixture.

‘You weren’t the only one thinking that,’ Dyer said when I spoke to him on Sunday. ‘After they scored their second goal, the Yeovil players started doing the Jacko Moonwalk. I was looking at them thinking, “you boys might have gone a bit early with that”.’

He was right about that. Dyer and his team had the last laugh. Southend scored three goals in the last 24 minutes to win the game 3-2. Don’t Stop ‘Til You Get Enough, as somebody once sang.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis visits Olympiacos star in hospital after horror leg break
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis has paid a visit to his star striker, Ayoub El Kaabi, in hospital after the Olympiacos player suffered a brutal leg break during his side's Greek Super League match on Saturday.

El Kaabi, who collected the Golden Boot in the Greek top flight last season for the second time since joining the club in 2023, was hospitalised after suffering the potentially career-ending injury against Volos.

The 33-year-old Morocco international had been charging towards the opposition goal at the end of the first half when Volos goalkeeper Marios Siampanis blocked his path and threw himself in front of the striker, catching him on the leg.

The floored El Kaabi raised his arm to signal to the bench that he needed urgent medical attention, while his agonised screams echoed around the stadium before he was stretchered off. Siampanis was seen covering his face with his gloves.

Nottingham Forest owner and Olympiacos president Marinakis showed his support for El Kaabi, posting a picture on social media by his bedside.

He captioned the post: 'Ayoub, wishing you a strong recovery and all the strength in the world!

Nottingham Forest owner and Olympiacos president Marinakis showed his support for El Kaabi, posting a picture on social media by his bedside

El Kaabi, who collected the Golden Boot in the Greek top flight last season, was hospitalised after suffering the potentially career-ending injury on the weekend

'You are strong, you are a winner, and I am certain that you will overcome this challenge as well. The surgery went very well, and now the most important thing is your recovery, so that you can come back even stronger.

'I want you to know that the entire Olympiacos family is by your side. We will make sure you have the very best care at every stage of your recovery, and we will be there for anything you may need.

'And one more thing: we want you to know that you are, and will always remain, a member of our family for as long as you want. Forever.

'Stay strong and positive. Everything will be fine, and soon you will be back with us, stronger and always a winner!'

According to his own account, El Kaabi has already undergone surgery on his broken leg.

On Instagram, he wrote: 'The procedure performed by our Olympiacos team doctor was successful. I thank our president, the coach, the players, and the support staff for their support.

'It means a great deal to me. Thanks also to our amazing Olympiacos fans for every message and every prayer. I could feel your love even from afar and am truly grateful for this blessing. God willing, I will return stronger.'

Record 48-time champions Olympiacos are looking to reclaim their crown this season after losing the title to AEK Athens last term.

They are currently third in the league after the opening three matches, two points behind leaders Panetolikos.

Sports.title: 'Can't believe he is alive': Praise for hero racing driver who saved British rival from fireball
Sports.content:
The wife of the British racing driver whose Ferrari burst into flames says she cannot believe he is not dead – and credits his rival who rushed to his rescue for keeping him alive.

Ollie Millroy, 36, had been racing in a China GT event at Shanghai International Circuit when two cars smashed into his Ferrari while navigating a bend.

In video footage of the incident, Millroy's vehicle is seen spiralling off the track while aggressive flames and huge plumes of smoke billow above it.

Rival Dutch driver Loek Hartog is then seen pulling up beside the wreckage before hurriedly unbuckling his seat belt and jumping out – sacrificing his chances of winning in the process.

Millroy's wife Fern is at his hospital bedside in Shanghai and this morning gave an update on the father-of-three's condition while crediting Hartog with saving his life.

'Surgery went well yesterday,' Fern wrote. 'It took several hours, main work being his right hand. He now has metal along the entirety of his clavicle right side, metal inside his right hand, six broken ribs supported with a compression wrap and on high flow oxygen whilst his lung recovers.

Ollie Millroy's wife was amazed to see him alive after his fireball crash in Shanghai

The driver almost lost his life after a crash in the China GT sent his vehicle up in flames

Millroy was trapped and rescued from his burning car by Dutch driver Loek Hartog

'Tried to come off the oxygen but his O2 level was just too low. He is in great care at this fantastic hospital in Shanghai and we can't thank the staff here enough. More X Rays and CT tomorrow morning.

'I still can't believe he's alive, purely down to our real life superhero Loek Hartog.'

Ollie and Fern married in October 2021 and have three young children.

Through a camera near the driver's seat of Hartog's car, the 23-year-old can be seen desperately rummaging through the Ferrari's remains in a bid to free Millroy, who had become trapped in the fireball.

Hartog today wrote: 'Overwhelmed by the support from everyone over the past two days. I feel incredibly lucky to be part of a racing community that looks after each other the way this one does.

'Thank you for all the messages and support sent to Ollie, his wife and family, and also to me and my family. It really means a lot. I'm travelling back home now and honestly can't wait to be there. I'm feeling good for now, but there have naturally been a lot of thoughts running through my head over the past few days.

Ollie and Fern have been married since October 2021 and have three children

Fern hailed Millroy's rival Loek Hartog and credited him with saving her husband's life

'Most importantly, I want to make sure those thoughts and everything we've experienced are directed towards something constructive. In Ollie's words: making sure that no two people ever have to go through the same thing again in the future.'

From hospital, Millroy thanked the Dutchman for 'saving his life'.

He wrote: 'I am still alive tonight, entirely thanks to one man. Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshals or fire crews in sight, and risked his own life to get me out of the car.

'I don't remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and 1 hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life.

'One day I will tell our three kids this story and Loek will be the biggest superhero in history in their eyes too.

'I'm laying here tonight with five broken ribs, broken collar bone, broken hand and finger and a bruised lung, but it could have been much worse.

Hartog has been hailed as a 'superhero' for his 'selfless act' in saving his rival

'Thank you Loek. I owe you my life for your selfless act today.'

Hartog, meanwhile, posted on his own social media: 'When I saw a car turning into a huge fireball far ahead, there wasn't really a decision to make.

'From what I had seen, I genuinely believed the driver might not be able to get out by himself. I stopped, got out and went towards the car. There was never a moment of doubt.

'It was scary. There were moments where I didn't know I would actually be able to get Ollie out. But this isn't about what I did, and I'm sure many people in the same position would have reacted exactly the same way.'

Sports.title: Kevin Pietersen makes shock return to England setup as he's named 'specialist mentor' for World Cup build-up
Sports.content:
Kevin Pietersen makes shock return to England setup as he's named 'specialist mentor' for World Cup build-up

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kevin Pietersen has joined England's coaching staff on a white-ball consultancy building up to next year's World Cup.

Pietersen, 46, will work with the limited-overs teams as a specialist mentor, supporting head coach Brendon McCullum. He will start work next week when Harry Brook's side begins their twin series matches against Sri Lanka to end the English summer.

Regular coaching personnel Marcus Trescothick, Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor remain in their positions.

A T20 World Cup winner in 2010, Pietersen will also be involved in tours to Australia and South Africa this winter and then return for next summer's series with Pakistan and New Zealand, which will prepare England for the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa next autumn.

Kevin Pietersen is set to return to England in a mentor role

Pietersen said: 'Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment. We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad, and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential.

'To be a part of Brendon's think tank over the next 12 months is a fantastic opportunity, and I cannot wait to get started.'

The shock move comes a year after Pietersen held a similar role with Delhi in the Indian Premier League. Delhi finished fifth in the table but Pietersen did not return for 2026 citing a busy schedule.

The ECB believe that his upbringing in South Africa gives Pietersen’s unique perspective that will help the team in conditions in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

His recruitment is the latest in a line of ‘specialists’ signed up during Rob Key’s tenure as director of England men’s cricket: Mike Hussey was part of the support staff during the Twenty20 World Cup triumph in Australia in 2022 while Kieron Pollard took up a similar position in the 2024 event in the Caribbean, which resulted in an exit in the semi-finals.

Pietersen played 104 Tests and 173 white-ball games for England between 2004 and 2014

As far back as 11 years ago, England turned to Sri Lankan Mahela Jayawardene to help them understand the challenges of playing on the pitches of Asia.

‘I’ve got immense respect for KP and what he’s achieved in the game. He’s had an amazing impact on English cricket, so for someone with his experience, knowledge and stature to want to play a role with this team is a fantastic result,’ said McCullum.

‘I’m particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him. KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players.

'We’ve always respected each other and had a strong appreciation for what the other brings to the game, so I’m really looking forward to working together.’

The appointment of Pietersen, who won 275 international caps across all formats, comes a matter of weeks after another high-profile former England player, Andrew Flintoff, left his role as England Lions coach.

Brook was scheduled to work with Pietersen at last year’s IPL but pulled out of the tournament after prioritising his England commitments.

Sports.title: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc suffers 160mph crash - suspending F1's Italian Grand Prix - just after team-mate Lewis Hamilton raged at him forcing him off the track
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was left sitting in pain on the grass after suffering a dramatic 160mph crash at the start of the Italian Grand Prix.

The Ferrari favourite lost control of his car at the final bend, the Parabolica, on the second lap as he duelled with Oscar Piastri for fourth place.

Leclerc’s impact with the wall was severe with only a short portion of gravel to slow his trajectory into the hoardings, which he thudded side-on.

The Monegasque soon jumped out of the car but then sat disconsolately on the grass as he was comforted by a marshal before being taken away in the medical car. He was feeling his neck as he went for treatment. Ferrari said he had been released from the medical centre without injury.

The race was red-flagged and some fans in the grandstands cried at the huge blow for their team.

Charles Leclerc spins off at Monza's Parabolica turn and crashes into the barriers

Leclerc was seen with his head in his hands on the grass after the heavy smash which saw the Italian Grand Prix red-flagged

The two Ferraris came together with Hamilton, left, dropping several places as a result

By this point, Leclerc had already squeezed his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton on the second part of the opening Del Refillo chicane and was driving somewhat erratically. Hamilton was furious, saying: ‘Charles pushed me off.’

The seven-time world champion, who started fourth, fell down to tenth place.

George Russell was leading the race for Mercedes when the race was suspended after passing pole man Pierre Gasly on the main straight at the end of the first lap.

Leclerc’s stricken car was taken away by crane.

Organisers announced the race would resume at 2.39pm, UK time.

Off the track Game of Thrones star Nathalie Emmanuel was joined by EastEnders actor Ben Hardy at Monza with Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0%.

The pair were immersed in the action and had a tour of the F1 paddock and had access inside the Scuderia Ferrari HP garage, where they were pictured in front of Leclerc’s Ferrari.

Game of Thrones star Nathalie Emmanuel, 37, was at Monza with Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0%

Sports.title: New Brett Favre video leaves NFL fans worried about his health after divisive quarterback was diagnosed with Parkinson's
Sports.content:
NFL fans are concerned for Brett Favre's health after the iconic quarterback appeared in a new video over the weekend.

Favre, 56, revealed he has Parkinson's during a September 2024 congressional hearing but has kept details of his progress largely under wraps ever since.

However, the 1996 Super Bowl winner and three-time MVP recorded a video for the Green Bay Packers' Mexican fans ahead of the new NFL season which was posted on social media.

Fans quickly flooded the comments with their concerns for Favre and wished him well during his battle with the progressive brain disorder.

One commented: 'Very sad to see anyone fighting through this horrible disease. God bless him and his family. He was a great football player!'

Another added: 'He's the reason I fell in love with football, this is rough to watch.'

NFL fans are concerned for Brett Favre's health after he appeared in a new video

A third responded: 'Damn this is sad to see. Watching him play was something else.'

'Sad to see,' another wrote. 'He had a cannon for an arm.. fun to watch.'

One concerned onlooker declared it 'terrible,' while another added it was 'truly sad.'

Favre was known for his durability during his football career after registering an NFL-record streak of 297 consecutive starts, a figure that goes up to 321 if playoff games are included.

He won three straight MVP awards with Green Bay from 1995-97. Favre led the 1996 Packers to their first Super Bowl title in nearly three decades and brought them back to the Super Bowl the following year.

Favre was with Green Bay from 1992-2007 and also played for the Atlanta Falcons (1991), New York Jets (2008) and Minnesota Vikings (2009-10).

During an episode of his '4th and Favre' podcast back in December, Favre shared a rare update on his Parkinson's fight, admitting it does not entail what most people assume.

'I'm probably like most people – I thought there was just one Parkinson's and that was it. There's not. There's multiple, many forms of Parkinson's,' he said.' 'And I have what's called idiopathic, which is the most common.

Brett Favre has gone downhill fast pic.twitter.com/SDM0X7mplJ — Behold A Pale Horse (@BeholdPaleH0rse) September 6, 2026

The 56-year-old announced he is battling the progressive brain disorder in September 2024

The former Packers quarterback won three straight MVP awards with Green Bay from 1995-97

'I think the other thing most people think when they hear of Parkinson's is they think of shaking. I get from time to time, "Oh you must not be too bad because you don't shake." I have very little shaking. I have some, but it's pretty rare.

'But as I've learned, the Parkinson's that I have has three different characteristics. One of those three you'll have as the dominant side effect. It's cognitive and memory is one. Shaking and tremors is two. And rigidity and stiffness is three. I major in the rigidity and stiffness.'

The Green Bay Packers icon continued: 'So, when I wake up in the morning before I take my medicine, I’m as close to a 2 by 4 as you could possibly get. And once I take my medicine, it’s like the muscles and the joints kind of ease their grip on me.

'When I get fatigued, mainly toward the end of the day, I do shake a little bit. My cognitive memory – part of it, right now it’s OK.

'As you well know, there’s no cure. I hear from time to time, "Well, they’re five years away from a cure." I hope that that’s the case. But I’m not holding my breath.'

Sports.title: Chelsea are being held back by a glaring gap that will haunt them until January: They may have banked £125m for Enzo Fernandez but that big bag of cash is no help on the pitch, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
It was almost as if Arsenal were rubbing it in, replacing Myles Lewis-Skelly with Martin Zubimendi to join Declan Rice in their midfield and with Bruno Guimaraes unused among the substitutes.

Mikel Arteta had elite midfielders to spare. Xabi Alonso, meanwhile, finished this match with two right backs in Reece James and Malo Gusto trying to fill in centrally while trailing 2-1.

We know what went down on deadline day so do not need to repeat it in full here, but to summarise it in a sentence: Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez and signed nobody.

That made Arteta's 67th-minute substitution in his own midfield all the more intriguing. Chelsea were offered the chance to potentially sign Lewis-Skelly by intermediaries in the summer. They were interested in bringing in Zubimendi for a reunion with Alonso. They looked at multiple other midfielders, from Bournemouth’s Alex Scott to Roma’s Manu Kone to Monaco’s Lamine Camara.

They signed none of those names. With Moises Caicedo still sidelined, Jordan Henderson not ready and Alonso seemingly lacking some trust in Valentin Barco – the 22-year-old Argentinian who arrived from sister side Strasbourg this summer – Chelsea started with James and Romeo Lavia. When Gusto replaced Lavia after an hour, it confirmed the latter has still yet to complete a competitive full 90 for this club.

Xabi Alonso finished this match with two right backs in Reece James and Malo Gusto trying to fill in centrally

Arsenal have a wealth of talent in their squad, and Bruno Guimaraes didn't even make it off the bench against Chelsea

It is a glaring gap which held Chelsea back here, and one which threatens to continue to haunt them until they get to January at least. They got £125million for Fernandez, which is mind-boggling money, but that big bag of cash is no help on the actual pitch when unspent.

Chelsea have made a habit of scoring early. They took the lead against Fulham after 31 seconds, Brighton after 219 seconds, and Arsenal after 77 seconds. If the team mentality suddenly needs to shift because they have something to protect, that is harder to do without the appropriate players.

(Unlike Chelsea) Arsenal are all singing from the same hymn sheet

Chelsea’s analysts had seen this goal from Arsenal before. It was a copy and paste from their Community Shield victory over Manchester City. Christos Tzolis moves inside from the right, passes centrally, Martin Odegaard meets it and scores with only the goalkeeper in his way.

Arsenal looked like champions who knew exactly what to do under Arteta, and Chelsea like challengers still trying to understand what Alonso wants from them.

It was a carefully orchestrated move from Arteta. Alonso’s centre backs were preoccupied, Maxence Lacroix with Riccardo Calafiori after the left back had charged forward into the inside channel and Wesley Fofana with Kai Havertz. Odegaard was able to drift inside to meet Tzolis’s pass which was dummied by Havertz and score beyond a helpless Emiliano Martinez.

Speaking of Martinez, had Robert Sanchez conceded Arsenal’s equaliser from Havertz, there would have been untold criticism on social media of the Spaniard. The Argentinian may have been ever so slightly unsighted, but he will know that he should not have been beaten so easily.

Had Robert Sanchez conceded Arsenal’s equaliser from Havertz, there would have been untold criticism on social media of the Spaniard

MacPhee's magic touch

Chelsea's set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had a plan for how to deal with Arsenal at corners.

When Arteta’s side won their first, Chelsea immediately sent four players up the pitch. Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer stood on the halfway line while Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto were 15 yards deeper.

It forced Arsenal to send four of their own men back to mark them and cleared the congestion in the box.

Do not be surprised if we see others copy this tactic soon.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
