World.title: Fuel prices soar in Hungary: Diesel hits 4-year high – what does the government say about fuel price caps?
World.content:
Hungarian motorists are facing another sharp increase in fuel prices, with diesel reaching its highest level in almost four years. Further price rises could follow as the situation in the Middle East pushes up oil prices, but the government says it has no plans to bring back the previous fuel price cap.

Fuel prices have jumped significantly at Hungarian petrol stations, with the average price of 95 petrol rising by HUF 8 per litre and diesel by HUF 9 compared with Friday. According to the latest figures from Holtankoljak, the national average prices now stand at:

95 petrol: HUF 617 per litre (EUR 1.7)

HUF 617 per litre (EUR 1.7) Diesel: HUF 697 per litre (EUR 1.92)

The latest diesel price is particularly striking: it has not been this high since December 2022, according to Portfolio.

Why are fuel prices rising?

Several factors are putting pressure on the Hungarian fuel market. The restrictions on Russian diesel exports, production disruptions at Russian refineries and escalating tensions in the Middle East are all contributing to higher prices.

The renewed conflict in the Middle East could prove particularly important in the coming days. Eszter Bujdos, head of the Hungarian Mineral Oil Association, said there is a strong possibility of further increases because the latest attacks have not yet been fully reflected in market prices.

The price of Brent crude is currently around USD 95 a barrel, and it could climb further if tensions continue to escalate. That could quickly translate into higher prices at Hungarian filling stations.

If you missed it: Hungary fuel prices face first major test as oil climbs and government rules out costly cap

Government rules out bringing back the price cap

Despite growing pressure on motorists, the government does not currently intend to reintroduce the protected fuel price that was previously used to limit pump prices.

János Bóka, the former minister responsible for European Union affairs, has pointed to previous statements by Prime Minister Péter Magyar and Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány during the election campaign regarding fuel prices and price protection.

The previous government introduced a fuel price cap during the energy crisis, setting the protected price at HUF 595 per litre for petrol and HUF 615 for diesel. Today’s averages are already more than HUF 10 above the former petrol cap and more than HUF 70 above the former diesel price.

The government is nevertheless looking for ways to ease the burden on motorists. Magyar has discussed the problem with István Kapitány as part of talks about the challenges facing Hungary’s economy and energy sector. However, the prime minister has indicated that simply restoring a price cap would not be the preferred solution.

The government wants measures that would reduce the pressure on drivers without creating fuel shortages or costing the state budget tens of billions of forints every month.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Could taxes be changed instead?

Energy expert Attila Holoda has suggested that changing the tax burden on fuel could be one possible solution, ATV reports. If the government wants to protect motorists from international price shocks, it could potentially adjust the tax structure rather than impose a fixed retail price.

However, such measures would have their limits. If international fuel prices and the price of crude oil rise substantially, Hungary is likely to feel the impact just like neighbouring countries. In other words, government intervention could soften the blow, but it cannot completely isolate Hungarian motorists from developments on global energy markets.

Hundreds of small petrol stations under pressure

The latest price surge is also raising concerns about the survival of smaller, independent petrol stations. The Association of Independent Petrol Stations (FBSZ) has sent an open letter to Prime Minister Péter Magyar, warning that the situation in Hungary’s fuel retail sector has become increasingly difficult.

The association estimates that 600–700 mainly Hungarian-owned family businesses could be directly affected and some are already approaching insolvency.

According to the organisation, the difference between fuel prices and the wholesale and retail pricing structure set by MOL is currently insufficient to cover the operating costs of many smaller businesses. The FBSZ is calling for immediate government intervention and a comprehensive investigation of the Hungarian fuel market.

It also claims that international fuel supply, particularly diesel, has become highly unstable, with two major traders reportedly announcing restrictions or suspensions affecting supplies to certain independent filling stations.

Why price caps can hurt smaller stations

Independent petrol stations can be particularly vulnerable when the government intervenes directly in retail fuel prices. During previous price-cap measures, so-called “white stations” (independent, unbranded filling stations) faced intense pressure because their margins were squeezed while consumers often preferred larger branded chains, according to Telex.

Major fuel companies have deeper financial reserves and can potentially absorb losses for longer. Smaller, family-owned operators have much less room to manoeuvre. This creates a difficult balancing act for the government: protecting motorists from rising prices while avoiding measures that could drive independent petrol stations out of business or create shortages.

Diesel could stay more expensive than petrol

There is also concern that diesel prices could remain elevated for an extended period. Bujdos said motorists should not expect a diesel shortage, but warned that supply risks in the diesel market have increased, making the fuel more expensive to secure.

She expects diesel to remain available but believes its price could stay high. The gap between petrol and diesel prices may eventually narrow, but diesel is expected to remain more expensive than petrol for the rest of the year. That would have consequences well beyond motorists.

A large proportion of road freight is carried by diesel-powered vehicles. If diesel prices remain high, transport companies could eventually pass their higher costs on to customers, potentially contributing to higher prices for goods across the Hungarian economy.

World.title: Magyar government targets thousands of billions in Orbán-era private equity deals
World.content:
Hungary’s new government is reviewing state contracts worth thousands of billions of forints involving companies owned through private equity funds, potentially putting some of the biggest business deals of the previous era under scrutiny.

The Tisza government has begun examining contracts signed under the previous government with companies whose ownership is linked to private equity funds, according to a report by 24.hu. The review follows new transparency rules that have made it much harder for the real beneficiaries behind Hungary’s private equity funds to remain hidden from the public.

Since 5 August, the owners and beneficiaries behind private equity funds can no longer remain anonymous in major state-related transactions. Those who fail to make the required disclosures can be barred from applying for new public funding and from signing new contracts with the state.

The changes are already having tangible consequences for several companies linked to Hungary’s previous political establishment.

Photo: MTI

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Mészáros-linked companies already hit by funding losses

One of the most prominent names affected is billionaire businessman Lőrinc Mészáros, whose business empire expanded dramatically during the previous government’s years in power. According to 24.hu, several major financial opportunities connected to Mészáros-linked companies have already fallen through. Among them:

Opus Titász Zrt. lost out on around HUF 60 billion in EU funding in connection with a major electricity network development programme.

Gallicoop Zrt., a turkey-processing company, had HUF 33 billion in support withdrawn after authorities determined that the ownership structure did not meet the relevant requirements.

A company linked to one of the private equity funds also had to repay more than HUF 2 billion to the state after profits had allegedly been extracted before the state took over the road toll system.

The Gallicoop case is particularly revealing. The Agriculture Ministry reportedly argued that the funding had been improperly awarded because the company was owned by private equity funds, making it impossible to establish the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner. But these cases may prove to be only the beginning.

If you missed it: Hungarian police seize thousands of documents in investigation into state Eximbank deals

The HUF 24,000 billion motorway deal is next

The biggest question concerns Hungary’s 35-year motorway concession, estimated to be worth around HUF 24,000 billion (EUR 66 billion).

The concession has already attracted scrutiny in Brussels, where an infringement procedure is under way. Meanwhile, Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy has repeatedly indicated that the Hungarian government intends to examine the agreement in detail.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar has also singled out the motorway concession as a prime example of what he calls “public money devouring”. That could put the concessionaire, MKIF Zrt., under scrutiny.

The company has an unusual ownership structure: seven private equity funds appear among its owners. These funds have been associated with the business interests of Mészáros and his long-standing business partner László Szíjj, although the private equity fund structure has historically made it difficult for the public to identify the ultimate beneficiaries. The new transparency rules could change that.

State has already paid HUF 1,024 billion

Another controversial aspect of the motorway concession is the amount of money already paid by the state. According to figures cited by Vitézy, the Hungarian state has paid HUF 1,024 billion (EUR 2.83 billion) to MKIF so far, which is more than the value of the work completed by the concession company.

Critics argue that instead of reducing the burden on the state budget, the arrangement effectively allows the state to pre-finance the private operator while shielding it from significant risks. That is likely to make the concession one of the most politically sensitive elements of the government’s wider review.

4iG and the waste concession also examined

The investigation is not limited to the motorway business. A number of companies within the 4iG Group also have private equity funds among their owners, and the new government is examining the relationship between the state and 4iG as well.

The waste management concession is also undergoing a comprehensive review. In this case, however, the concession is operated by the MOL Group, rather than through the same type of private-equity-fund ownership structure. The government’s approach suggests that contracts and concessions established during the previous era could face significantly greater scrutiny than before.

Private equity funds face a choice

The new rules could force the beneficiaries behind Hungary’s private equity funds into an uncomfortable position. They can either reveal who ultimately benefits from their lucrative state-linked businesses, or risk losing access to future public contracts and funding.

The scale of the contracts involved is enormous, with the motorway concession alone estimated at HUF 24,000 billion.

World.title: Former PM Orbán congratulates German AfD on ‘landslide victory’
World.content:
Former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has celebrated a major election breakthrough for Germany’s far-right AfD, calling its result in Saxony-Anhalt a “huge night for Germany and Europe” and declaring: “This is just the beginning.”

Orbán was quick to congratulate the Alternative for Germany (AfD) after Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt, where the party secured around 43.8 per cent of the vote, according to preliminary results.

“Congratulations to Alice Weidel, Ulrich Siegmund, and the entire AfD on their landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt. Buckle up! This is just the beginning!” Orbán wrote on X.

The former Hungarian prime minister has been an outspoken supporter of the AfD. As early as 2025, he described the party as “the future”, signalling his belief that Germany’s political landscape was undergoing a major transformation.

A huge night for Germany and Europe! Congratulations to @Alice_Weidel, @UlrichSiegmund and the entire @AfD on their landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt! Buckle up. This is just the beginning! 💪 — Orbán Viktor (@PM_ViktorOrban) September 6, 2026

If you missed it: Far-right AfD co-leader: Hungary and Orbán model for Germany

AfD dominates in eastern Germany

The scale of the AfD’s result is striking. The party won roughly 43.8 per cent of the vote, far ahead of the centre-right CDU, which took around 17.2 per cent.

The Left Party received 8.6 per cent, while the Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens each secured around 9 per cent. The Greens improved on their previous result, while the newly formed Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) was hovering around the five per cent threshold.

Despite its huge lead, however, the AfD does not have an outright majority. Preliminary projections indicate that the party will hold around 39 of the 83 seats in the state parliament.

That means the AfD cannot govern alone and the formation of the next state government remains uncertain.

A historic breakthrough for the far right

Still, the election represents a major milestone in German politics. Saxony-Anhalt, a state of around 2.1 million people in eastern Germany, has become the focus of international attention because the AfD’s result raises the prospect of the party taking control of a German state government.

The election was particularly significant because voters and political observers were watching to see whether AfD could win an absolute majority and potentially secure its first state premiership. If the other parties cooperate, they could still prevent the AfD from forming a government despite its commanding electoral lead.

According to Telex, the result also carries historical significance: it marks the first time since the Second World War that a far-right party has come close to taking control of a German state government on the strength of such a dominant electoral result.

Salvini also celebrates AfD success

Orbán was not the only prominent European politician to welcome the result. Italian Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini also described the AfD’s performance as a sweeping success, arguing that the party had prevailed despite what he called the left’s continued attempts to “stoke fears” and promote catastrophic scenarios.

World.title: Hungary’s annual grave-digging contest makes headlines in US media
World.content:
Grave digging is not usually a spectator sport, but a professional competition in northern Hungary has managed to attract attention far beyond the country’s borders. Nineteen teams raced against the clock in Nyergesújfalu – and the unusual contest eventually made its way into the mainstream media.

The ninth national grave-digging competition was held at the New Public Cemetery in Nyergesújfalu, in Komárom-Esztergom County, bringing together professional cemetery workers to test their speed, endurance and technical skills.

A total of 19 teams took part in this year’s event. Competitors faced unusually hard, dry ground, strong winds and clouds of dust, while Index reported that hail also interrupted the competition.

The conditions meant that shovels were not always enough: some teams had to turn to pickaxes to make progress through the hardened soil.

The event is organised by the Hungarian Cemetery Maintenance and Operators Association (MTFE), which says the competition is intended not only to test professional ability but also to draw attention to a job that rarely receives much public recognition.

Two hours to dig a regulation-sized grave

The rules are surprisingly precise:

Each team must dig a grave measuring two metres long, 80 centimetres wide and 1.6 metres deep, with no more than two hours available for the task.

Digging a larger hole is permitted, although it costs competitors valuable time. A grave smaller than the specified dimensions is not accepted. Safety regulations also restrict how the teams can work. Only one person may be inside the grave at any given time, while their partner can manage the excavated soil from above but cannot enter the pit at the same time.

The annual grave digging competition Photo: MTFE / Facebook

This year’s conditions made meeting the time limit particularly difficult. According to a local report, only three teams completed the excavation stage within two hours.

And digging is only half the challenge. After a short break, the teams must fill the grave again and create the burial mound. The final result therefore takes into account both the excavation and the quality of the refilling work.

Safety rules

For safety reasons, only one member of each team may work inside the grave at a time.

The other team member may handle and arrange the excavated soil, but is not allowed to enter the grave.

This means the pair cannot work side by side in the pit, for example with one using a pickaxe while the other digs.

Competitors who leave the designated competition area are not permitted to return later.

If you missed it: Budapest Half Marathon breaks participation record with runners from 117 countries

Defending champions win again

The overall victory went to Paraklétosz Nonprofit Kft. from Hajdúböszörmény, whose team successfully defended its title.

The winners completed the digging stage in 1 hour, 21 minutes and 44 seconds.

Imre Lődi and Zsolt Krucsai, representing the Csongrád County funeral services company, finished second with a time of 1 hour, 32 minutes and 38 seconds. Their employer said the two men were experienced colleagues whose familiarity with working together was visible throughout the competition.

The field was not exclusively Hungarian either: a Russian duo also entered and finished sixth. According to Index, the winning team received HUF 200,000 in prize money.

Hungarian contest makes headlines in America

What began as a specialist professional event soon gained a much larger audience. The Associated Press reported from the Hungarian competition, and its story was subsequently carried by a range of US outlets, including ABC News and NewsNation, as well as several regional television stations.

Organisers have also said the competition can help break down some of the taboos surrounding death and give funeral-sector workers an opportunity to receive recognition for their work. The Hungarian contest has attracted foreign interest before. Previous editions have included grave diggers from countries including Serbia, Czechia and Russia.

World.title: Budapest’s hottest neighbourhoods are nearly 7°C warmer as mayor warns air conditioning is not the answer
World.content:
Budapest’s increasingly hot summers are exposing a striking temperature divide across the city, with leafy districts measuring almost 7°C cooler than some of the most densely built-up neighbourhoods. Mayor Gergely Karácsony says the answer should be more greenery, shading and passive cooling rather than simply installing more air conditioners.ú

Karácsony opened his Sunday Facebook post with a joke from a City Hall presentation: a slide supposedly showing the hottest surfaces in the universe featured the Sun, a quasar, a steaming iron – and Budapest’s Baross Square in summer. The comparison may be tongue-in-cheek, but the underlying data are not.

Satellite thermal sensors examined Budapest on 32 summer and four winter occasions between 2013 and 2025, measuring surface temperatures at a resolution of 30 metres at around 9:30 in the morning. Rather than air temperature, the measurements show how hot surfaces such as asphalt, roofs, parks and other urban areas become.

According to Karácsony, a positive urban heat island effect was detectable on 24 of the 32 summer days studied, or 75% of the observations. Budapest was between 0.5°C and 2.6°C warmer than its surroundings.

Nearly 7°C separates Budapest’s coolest and hottest districts

The differences inside the capital are considerably larger. The lowest average surface temperatures were recorded in the greener 2nd and 12th districts, while the highest were found in the densely built-up 6th and 7th districts. The difference between the two extremes reached 6.8°C at the same time of day.

Natural and heavily built-up areas also have strikingly different effects. According to the figures cited by the mayor, the Danube cools its immediate surroundings by around 6.6°C, while the area around Budapest Airport is approximately 5°C warmer.

The findings reinforce a familiar urban pattern: trees, vegetation and water help absorb and dissipate heat, while concrete, asphalt and large built surfaces store it.

If you missed it: PM Magyar gives fresh update on Paks as major Danube intervention advances

Karácsony warns of an air-conditioning ‘vicious circle’

Air conditioning may provide immediate relief indoors, but Karácsony argued that widespread mechanical cooling can make the wider urban problem worse. He cited a US modelling study in which waste heat released by air-conditioning units increased average night-time temperatures by more than 1°C in some locations.

That creates a feedback loop: hotter nights increase demand for cooling, while the air conditioners themselves release more heat outside.

In Hungary, 27% of homes had air conditioning in 2022, according to census data quoted by Karácsony, although he said the real proportion is now likely to be significantly higher.

The differences between Hungarian cities were already substantial at the time. In Szeged, 46% of homes had air conditioning, compared with 31% in Győr and 19% in Miskolc.

Within Budapest, the 13th district had the highest rate, partly because of its newer housing stock. By contrast, the particularly hot 6th and 7th districts have older buildings and fewer air-conditioned homes.

Heatwave pushed electricity demand up 23%

The growing use of cooling systems is also placing pressure on Hungary’s electricity network. Karácsony said daily electricity demand during the heatwave at the end of June was 23% higher than in the days immediately beforehand.

The problem becomes particularly acute at night. Urban buildings and paved surfaces release the heat accumulated during the day, keeping temperatures elevated even after sunset. At the same time, solar panels stop producing electricity while demand for air conditioning remains high.

Karácsony said Budapest’s response to extreme heat should focus on trees, green spaces, shading and passive cooling, rather than simply installing more air conditioners.

He also called for building renovations that combine insulation with measures such as light-coloured or green roofs, which can help prevent homes from overheating during prolonged hot spells.

The mayor thinks that EU funding could support these broader renovation schemes, including Budapest’s Green Panel programme, and argued that climate adaptation should become a central part of future housing policy.

World.title: PM Magyar gives fresh update on Paks as major Danube intervention advances
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar has issued a fresh update on the emergency works near Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant, saying the project is progressing according to schedule and that the plant is operating steadily. His comments come amid growing criticism over riverbed erosion, environmental permitting and the way the government has handled one of Hungary’s most sensitive energy-security projects.

In a Facebook post on Sunday evening, Magyar said work between Paks and Dunaszentbenedek was advancing as planned and rejected suggestions that the intervention was running into serious trouble.

“None of the scare stories being spread by panic-mongering hacks are true,” Magyar wrote.

According to the prime minister, the deepening of the riverbed is an expected process during construction of the bottom sill, while specialists are continuously adding material to the riverbed and strengthening the protective structure. Magyar said nearly 70,000 cubic metres of rock had already been placed as part of the works.

“The Paks Nuclear Power Plant is operating steadily,” he added.

He also said construction of a new port promised to Dunaszentbenedek on the opposite bank of the Danube was progressing well. Magyar had visited Dunaszentbenedek on Saturday, where he attended the local village day and met residents. He returned to the Paks issue with Sunday evening’s post.

Concerns raised over the Danube works

Magyar’s reassurances come after recent reports raised questions about the effects of the intervention on the Danube riverbed.

Átlátszó reported that the narrowing of the river during construction had accelerated the current around the unfinished bottom sill, contributing to significant erosion in parts of the riverbed. Critics have questioned whether the scale of the changes could complicate the remainder of the project.

If you missed it: New Danube barrier is completed ahead of schedule, Paks reaches full capacity

The government has rejected suggestions that the works are out of control. Magyar has argued that faster water flow and some deepening of the riverbed were anticipated consequences of narrowing the channel during construction, and that engineers are continuously reinforcing the affected area.

Environmental concerns have also been raised over the project, particularly about its possible effects downstream. The government, however, maintains that the intervention is being carried out in line with environmental and nature-protection requirements.

Works continue after first phase completed

The latest update comes just over a week after the first phase of the temporary bottom sill was completed across the Danube. At the time, Magyar said around 43,000 cubic metres of rock had been used in just 17 days, while the Paks Nuclear Power Plant had returned to full capacity.

Sunday’s figures show that construction has continued at considerable pace. Magyar now says nearly 70,000 cubic metres of rock have been incorporated into the river works, as specialists continue to reinforce the riverbed and the structure itself.

The prime minister also stressed that Paks is operating steadily, while work on the new port at Dunaszentbenedek is progressing on the opposite bank.

The project nevertheless remains under scrutiny over changes to the riverbed and its environmental impact. Magyar’s latest message was aimed squarely at those concerns, insisting that the observed deepening of the riverbed had been anticipated and was being addressed as part of the ongoing construction.

World.title: Kosovo Man Pleads Not Guilty to Spying for Serbia
World.content:
Fatmir Sheholli at the Pristina Basic Court on Monday, September 7, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

Former political commentator Fatmir Sheholli pleaded not guilty to carrying out espionage and blackmail for the Serbian intelligence agency, BIA, on Monday in a pre-trial hearing at the Pristina Basic Court.

Sheholli, former head of the Pristina-based Institute for Advancing Interethnic Relations, was arrested in October 2025 and has been in detention ever since.

He is accused of acting on instructions from the BIA to collect and pass on information about Kosovo’s institutions, political activities, and security situation.

Judge Avni Syla informed the accused and his counsel that they had the right to challenge the evidence and request the dismissal of the indictment within a 30-day period. However, Sheholli’s lawyer, Mentor Neziri, said his client had waived this right and requested that the court proceed immediately to the trial phase.

According to the indictment, seen by BIRN, Sheholli worked for the BIA until his arrest in October 2025, “collecting and passing on information about Kosovo’s political activities, security situation, and state institutions”.

It alleges that Sheholli carried out the orders of Bojan Dimic, who the prosecution claims is a senior BIA official. Some of the material Sheholli shared, according to the prosecution, concerned Serb-owned properties in Kosovo, business activities, and the functioning of Kosovo’s institutions.

According to the indictment, on August 5, 2025, Sheholli sent a document labelled “Top Secret 2” to a person identified as Viktor Makedonija, outlining a covert political and strategic plan involving influential figures in Kosovo in fields such as sports, music, media and politics, that the prosecution claims aimed to assist Islamic radicalisation in Kosovo and the region and destabilize the country.

They allegedly aimed to portray Kosovo as a radicalised and extremist state, damaging its international standing and influencing Western countries’ positions towards it.

The prosecution further alleges that in September 2025, Sheholli gave material obtained from Dimic to journalist Milaim Zeka for publication through his “Pa Rrotulla” TV programme, including the timing of publication, for which Zeka allegedly received 1,000 euros.

Sheholli denied that Zeka knew about his direct communication with Dimic. He also told the prosecution that Zeka had requested 3,000 to 4,000 euros for translating, editing, and publishing the material.

The prosecution claims that one month after his arrest, Sheholli told his visitors at the Gjilan/Gnilanje Detention Centre “that he received a USB drive, transcripts, and 5,000 euros from a person in North Mitrovica, materials which, according to him, contained intercepted communications and information concerning abuse of office and corruption.

‘He stated that he had handed the materials to journalist Milaim Zeka for publication, giving him 1,000 for publishing them,” it added.

Zeka has not responded to BIRN’s request for comment.

In another allegation, based on a photograph of a document found on Sheholli’s phone, the prosecution alleges that he was involved in a plan to discredit Kosovo’s acting Prime Minister Albin Kurti.

The document found on Sheholli’s phone relates to the time when Kurti was a political prisoner in Nis, Serbia from 1999 to 2001. The prosecution claims that the document, which Sheholli allegedly planned to use against Kurti, was allegedly drawn up by Serbia’s state security structures in 2001 and was signed by the head of the third sector of Serbia’s state security service.

Sheholli is also charged with blackmailing a Kosovo Albanian businessman, Arben Jetullahu, between 2022 and December 2025, demanding more than 13,000 euros, threatening that video recordings and other information damaging to the businessman would be made public if he refused.

In December 2021, a BIRN investigation found that RAD, a company owned by Radule Stevic, a Kosovo Serb businessman blacklisted by the US for alleged corruption, had been winning government tenders in Kosovo’s Serb-dominated north and then subcontracting construction work to ethnic Albanian-owned firms, including one owned by Jetullahu.

In October 2025, BIRN reported that former KIA director Driton Gashi spent more than 1 million euros from the Special Operational Fund, including 500,000 euros for which the recipient could not be identified. However, the agency’s chief inspector, Kujtim Shala, confirmed that the other 500,000 had been received by Sheholli.

This is the sixth case at the Pristina Basic Court related to charges of espionage for Serbian intelligence agency in the past two years.

In August, the Pristina Basic Court ordered 30 days of detention for Fehim Sali, who has reportedly admitted working for Serbia’s BIA, which allegedly paid him to identify other potential recruits.

In June, the same court sentenced a Kosovo Albanian man, Hysri Selimi, a former Islamic State member, to six years in prison for espionage. In May, the court sentenced Kosovo Police lieutenant Bojan Jevtic to six years’ imprisonment for espionage. Jevtic was found guilty of leaking information about the Kosovo police to the BIA.

In April, the court sentenced Jelena Djukanovic, an employee of the OSCE Mission in Kosovo, to six years’ imprisonment for spying for Serbia by providing internal OSCE information related to the situation mainly in the Serb-majority municipalities in the north of Kosovo.

In June 2025, the court sentenced Aleksandar Vlajic to five years’ imprisonment for espionage as the BIA’s resident agent.

World.title: Belgrade Pride March Marks 25 Years with Call for Tolerance
World.content:
Serbia’s annual LGBTQ+ Pride March took to the streets of the capital Belgrade on Saturday, with participants waving rainbow flags as they walked through the city centre.

The march – held 25 years after the first Belgrade Pride was attacked by homophobic thugs – was held under police protection and passed off without incident. Part of Belgrade Pride Week, it had the slogan “There Is Room for All of Us” – the same as the first march in 2001.

Participants carried banners reading “Visibility is not propaganda”, “God loves everyone” and “Queer students are winning too” – a refence to the slogan used by students who have led anti-government protests since 2024.

World.title: Nearing EU Accession, Montenegro Targets Money Behind Organised Crime
World.content:
Parliament in Montenegro adopted a law on September 3 allowing for the confiscation of assets worth at least 50,000 euros in ongoing cases of alleged organised crime, but experts questioned the state’s capacity to implement it.

Organised crime, notably cigarette smuggling, flourished in Montenegro in the 1990s during the collapse of socialist Yugoslavia; the authorities say they are determined to root it out as Podgorica eyes accession to the European Union, but experts say it’s one thing to change laws, and another thing entirely to use them.

Previously, authorities were able to confiscate assets worth at least 5,000 euros if there was a reasonable suspicion that those assets were acquired through criminal activity, the owner could not prove their legal origin, and that the person had been convicted of a criminal offence.

That remains, but now, in cases of organised crime, assets worth at least 50,000 euros can be seized permanently as soon as charges are confirmed by a court or a main hearing has been scheduled, providing that the court is satisfied that the proceedings have shown the assets were acquired by criminal means.

Previously, in all cases, assets could only be confiscated after a criminal conviction.

World.title: Serbia’s Spyware Abuse Escalates as Students Targeted in Election Run-Up
World.content:
As Serbia heads towards a snap parliamentary election, members of the country’s student-led protest movement and opposition politicians challenging the government of President Aleksandar Vucic have been targeted with some of the world’s most intrusive surveillance tools.

At least 14 people have been targeted with sophisticated spyware since the beginning of 2026, according to the Belgrade-based digital rights organisation SHARE Foundation, which described the cases as the largest documented wave of spyware targeting in Serbia to date. The targeting happened around tightly-contested local elections in March, and those affected included student activists, an opposition MP and a local councillor.

The investigation began after 12 people contacted SHARE in August after receiving Apple notifications warnings that they had been targeted with mercenary spyware. Less than two years after the Serbian authorities’ use of domestically-developed spyware NoviSpy was exposed, SHARE researchers in collaboration with the Citizen Lab and Amnesty International found a newly engineered version on students’ phones, alongside the first confirmed successful infection of a member of Serbia’s student protest movement by Pegasus spyware.

Investigators found evidence of a zero-click iMessage attack dating from December 2025 and January 2026, pointing to the highly intrusive Pegasus malware produced by Israel’s NSO Group. Such an infection can give an attacker access to messages, photographs and other data, as well as the ability to activate a phone’s microphone and camera covertly.

World.title: Serbian, Bosnian Serb Officials Join Hundreds at Ratko Mladic Commemoration
World.content:
The man, who preferred to withhold his name, now lives in the Serbian capital. He decided to come along and pay tribute to Mladic, who he considers a “hero who defended his country” and who, in his view, Serbia “betrayed” when it extradited him to the UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague in 2011.

A large number of people with similar views, mostly men, gathered in front of the Army House before the commemoration began. Some of them were wearing T-shirts depicting Ratko Mladic, with messages expressing support for him.

Three men wearing identical T-shirts stood together and posed for journalists’ photos. As well as an image of Mladic, the shirts bear the phrases often used as a message of support for him: “General, are you afraid of anyone? ‘I fear no one but God.’”

World.title: Slaven Bilić Surprises with New Names in Croatia’s Nations League Squad
World.content:
Croatia head coach Slaven Bilić announced the squad list he’s counting on for the upcoming Nations League fixtures in September and October.

Croatia have four competitive matches in the space of 11 days ahead of them, and head coach Bilić will be relying on the following players for this “campaign”:

“Summer has passed, that period where I did a lot of thinking, a lot of talking. The time to gather has come, and I think we’re ready now. I talked a lot with the players, watched, thought it over, and arrived at the final list. This is a specific situation — it’s the first time we’ve had four Nations League matches in around ten days. I don’t want this to disrupt my work. We’ve gone with 23 + 3.”

Player list

GOALKEEPERS: Dominik Livaković (Barcelona), Dominik Kotarski (Dinamo), Ivor Pandur (Rangers)

DEFENDERS: Joško Gvardiol (Manchester City), Josip Juranović (Union Berlin), Josip Šutalo (Lazio), Luka Vušković (Brighton), Ivan Smolčić (Como), Josip Stanišić (Bayern), Martin Erlić (Midtjylland)

MIDFIELDERS: Luka Modrić (Milan), Mateo Kovačić (Manchester City), Mario Pašalić (Atalanta), Nikola Vlašić (Torino), Petar Sučić (Inter), Luka Sučić (Real Sociedad), Josip Mišić (Dinamo), Martin Baturina (Como)

FORWARDS: Ivan Perišić (PSV), Andrej Kramarić (Hoffenheim), Ante Budimir (Osasuna), Igor Matanović (Freiburg), Franjo Ivanović (Lens), Dion Drena Beljo (Dinamo), Marco Pašalić (Orlando City), Petar Musa (Dallas FC)

ON STANDBY: Karlo Letica (Luzern), Marin Pongračić (Fiorentina), Kristijan Jakić (Augsburg), Nikola Moro (Bologna), Lovro Majer (AEK), Toni Fruk (Rijeka)

Bilić’s debut on September 26th

The big news of the weekend just gone is that Luka Modrić has confirmed he will continue playing for Croatia.

Luka Modrić has made 202 appearances for Croatia to date, and will now work with Slaven Bilić again after 14 years.

The squad list also features some new names, while some players will lose the place they held in the national team’s previous campaigns.

As for the Nations League schedule, what lies ahead for Croatia is anything but easy.

Bilić’s side travel to Czechia on September 26th, then to Spain three days later.

Two home matches follow: against England on October 3rd and Spain on October 6th.

Croatia’s fixture schedule in Nations League Group A3:

26 September, 20:45: Czechia – Croatia

29 September, 20:45: Spain – Croatia

3 October, 18:00: Croatia – England (Rujevica Stadium, Rijeka)

6 October, 20:45: Croatia – Spain (Poljud Stadium, Split)

World.title: Nikola Šubić Zrinski – The Croat Who Stopped 100,000 Ottomans
World.content:
September the 7th, 2026 – Turning the clock all the way back to the 7th of September 1566, and we meet the famed Nikola Šubić Zrinski, the Croat who stopped 100,000 Ottomans, but lost his life during the final charge.

Nikola Šubić Zrinski was a Croatian nobleman, ban (viceroy) and soldier who lived during the 16th century and is remembered as a defender of Christianity throughout Europe. Index writes that he is best known for the Battle of Szigetvár, in which the sultan himself also lost his life. In Croatia, he holds additional importance because he elevated the Zrinski noble family to the status of the most powerful Croatian family of all.

he never shied away from battling the fearsome ottoman forces

He was born sometime during 1508. We don’t know exactly where he entered the world, but we know he had five brothers and sisters. His father was Nikola Šubić and his mother Jelena Karlović. Nikola’s political activity did not come only from the fact that he was a nobleman; the Karlović family had a long tradition of state functions. Nikola’s uncle Ivan Karlović later served as ban. The brave Zrinski was primarily a soldier. After finishing military school, Šubić joined the ongoing war and defended Vienna in 1529, at which time he was noticed by many nobles and military officials. After the siege he was rewarded with a golden chain and received a horse.

The conflict with the Ottomans only continued. When he inherited the estate in the Una valley in 1534, he also inherited the obligation to pay tribute to the Ottomans. Nikola truly did not want to pay tribute to the enemy, so he provoked a conflict over the fortress of Dubica in order to justify not paying the taxes.

habsburg or zapolya?

At the same time the Kingdom of Hungary was very unstable. After the death of Vladislav II Jagiellon at Mohács, the whole country split into two camps: one favoured the Habsburgs and wanted to bring them to power in Hungary and Croatia, while the other favoured the local Hungarian nobleman John Zápolya. Nikola Šubić Zrinski considered Ferdinand Habsburg the better and wiser choice, and he had already become acquainted with the Habsburgs during the siege of Vienna. That is why, on his own initiative, he decided to kill the nobleman Johann Katzianer, who had rejected the Habsburgs and sworn loyalty to Zápolya. He captured Katzianer’s fortress of Kostajnica, but soon handed it over to the Ottomans, from whom he expected retaliation for refusing to pay tribute.

the zrinskis head north…

From the 1540s on, he was given administration of the whole of Međimurje. He soon moved there, renovated the castle in Čakovec, and after a few years received the right to collect taxes himself and to settle serfs in the area. At the same time he became Ban of Croatia, a title he held until 1556. He left the “office” of ban because he was dissatisfied that he had failed to raise more funds for the fight against the Ottomans. He wanted someone more capable to take the position while he continued to wage war against the enemy. He immediately received the position of treasurer in Hungary (Hungarian nobles were inclined to give him whatever he wanted because he was highly respected even before Szigetvár) and fought the Ottomans twice. He believed he already knew their strategies well and rushed into war with them whenever possible.

the famous battle of Szigetvár

The next opportunity presented itself in 1566 when he was staying in the fortress of Szigetvár. Szigetvár is located in Hungary on the shortest route to Vienna. Suleiman the Magnificent led 100,000 men to capture Szigetvár and begin a new siege of Vienna. To them Szigetvár was just another miserable Christian fortress; the Ottomans conquered such places every other day. However, Suleiman the Magnificent was not prepared for what was about to happen. Around 2,000 men, mostly ethnic Croats, decided that the Ottomans would not pass here. As soon as Ottoman infantry approached the gates of Szigetvár, the defenders threw everything they could at them and the enemy withdrew. Szigetvár was constantly bombarded with cannonballs for a full month, and one did not walk in the inner courtyard because of the arrows that fell into the fortress without stopping.

The defenders ate all the food they had, then began to eat their own horses. They maintained their morale largely thanks to Nikola Šubić, who in his classic style still saw only victory. Then came 7 September 1566, and it was clear that that morning the Ottomans would break into the town. Nikola put on a hat and noble attire, left his knight’s armour aside, took his father’s sabre and bravely led his men into the final episode of that nightmare. All the defenders died that morning, and the Ottomans achieved their goal.

an extremely costly goal

But the goal was achieved at too great a cost. The Ottoman army should not have lost a fifth of its force on some stupid and unimportant fortress, nor should it have been delayed there for half the summer. To make matters worse, during the siege Suleiman the Magnificent died, so the army’s morale was weak and worthless. The army was soon recalled and headed home. Nothing came of a new siege of Vienna. The heroic defence of Szigetvár was the main topic of conversation throughout Europe in the following months. Everyone spoke about Nikola Šubić: from Roman and Spanish diplomats who claimed that God had sent him to save Vienna from the Muslims, to the French Cardinal Richelieu who called him “the saviour of Europe and the Christian world.”

His descendants continued to act politically and hold various positions in the new state, the Habsburg Monarchy. Nikola elevated the Zrinskis from an ordinary noble family to the most important family in Croatia. Their influence would mark the following period, right up to the Zrinski-Frankopan conspiracy of 1671.

Nikola Šubić Zrinski remains incredibly relevant to this very day. Legends of his defence of Szigetvár were retold to children in the following centuries, and when the awakening of nationalism began in the 19th century, Nikola became even more popular. Then the 1880 earthquake struck Zagreb and the city had to be rebuilt. About a hundred metres southeast of Zagreb’s main square, construction began on the most beautiful park in the city centre. The park would be named Zrinjevac, or Nikola Šubić Zrinski Square, further immortalising him.

World.title: Much More Than Tourism: Croatia’s New Zagreb-Beijing Connection
World.content:
September the 7th, 2026 – Croatia’s brand new Zagreb-Beijing connection by Air China means much more than just more tourism from Asia, with business and cultural ties implied.

On Friday at 09:47, fire engines stood ready as the “giant” Air China aircraft touched down on the runway of Zagreb’s Franjo Tuđman Airport. The majestic plane of the Chinese carrier completed the first, inaugural flight between Beijing, Bucharest and Zagreb. Katarina Kusec reports for Poslovni that the aircraft was welcomed with a water salute upon landing, while passengers and crew were greeted by a number of high-ranking officials. This flight marked the start of year-round services between the mentioned cities.

a bridge of friendship

Air China’s aircraft landed in Zagreb for the first time and thus began regular operations to Croatia, opening many doors for cooperation and travel. The new route will operate three times a week (Monday, Wednesday and Friday), and flights will continue year-round, including throughout winter. “Good day, welcome (Dobar dan, dobrodosli,” Qi Qianjin, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to Croatia, briefly addressed everyone in Croatian. He added that the new route represents much more than an air link between China and Croatia: “It’s a bridge of friendship that connects our peoples and develops potential for further bilateral cooperation in culture, tourism, trade… It will also reduce logistics costs and improve delivery efficiency.”

He emphasised that this is the first such flight in the history of the two countries, while recalling that, despite this, we have a long history of cultural exchanges and economic and trade ties dating back to the time of Marco Polo.

The new route connects Beijing and Zagreb via Bucharest, the capital of Romania. Operations will work as follows: passengers, for example, board in Zagreb and fly to Bucharest as they would to other Schengen countries. There is a three-hour stopover during which border formalities and passport checks are carried out, after which the journey continues to China. The procedure is the same for return flights, while luggage remains on the aircraft. The total flight time is around 14 hours and practically connects two ends of the world.

more opportunities for cooperation

“Today we’re celebrating not only a new air route, but also a new opportunity for cooperation between the two countries in the fields of tourism, business and culture. We look forward to the development of this partnership in the years to come. This new route expands our connections and links Croatia with one of the most dynamic markets,” said Nicolas Duthilleul, CEO and Member of the Board of Zagreb International Airport (MZLZ). He added that more than 4.7 million passengers passed through the airport last year and that he is convinced that with this new route China and Croatia gain more opportunities to grow even closer.

He also noted that travel opportunities have now expanded and that the airport has prepared additional information and signage in Chinese throughout the terminal for Chinese passengers so they can navigate more easily and feel more comfortable.

Air China is using wide-body Airbus A330-200 aircraft on the route. This first arrival brings yet another major global carrier to Zagreb and further expands the flight offer. The A330-200 has a capacity of 265 seats, while around 120 passengers arrived on this inaugural flight from Beijing via Bucharest to Zagreb. The arrival time suits everyone, as morning disembarkation allows them to continue their day normally with other flights or to head into the city very early.

In any case, this is a good foundation for the coming tourist years, and Monika Udovičić, State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport, also sees potential in it.

great results for croatian tourism

“Croatian tourism will again finish this year with very good results, but what is more important is that we are significantly investing efforts in sustainable tourism, and I think this is something that will resonate well on the Chinese market. They come to see our natural beauty and cultural landmarks. The main motive is not only sun and sea, but our natural beauty,” she said, adding that Croatia has never been closer to China and that this is not just a route, but a better connection between the two countries that is moving towards strengthening relations, friendship and business.

“On distant markets, presence is built continuously through better transport connectivity, promotion and long-term partnerships, and this route represents an important step in that direction. I believe this route will contribute to an even stronger positioning of Croatia on the Chinese market.”

After the official part and the welcome of the crew and passengers, a cake was cut and champagne was poured, because big and new things need to be celebrated. Six journalists from China also attended the ceremony, as well as representatives of tourist boards. Among the speakers were also State Secretary at the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure Tomislav Mihotić, Director of the Croatian National Tourist Board Kristjan Staničić, and many others.

World.title: The Guardian Names Cres Europe’s Best Hidden Gem
World.content:
September the 7th, 2026 – The Guardian has spotlighted gorgeous Cres, referring to it as Europe’s best hidden gem.

The influential Guardian was well and truly won over by the wilderness of the beautiful island of Cres and its crystal-clear sea, which we must protect if we want it to remain that way.

Morski reports that the very widely read British newspaper The Guardian published a selection of lesser-known European islands worth visiting. Among suggestions from numerous countries, Cres in the Kvarner archipelago took first place. Reader Rhiannon, whose recommendation was chosen as the best, particularly highlighted the island’s nature and its impressive griffon vultures.

The Guardian describes Cres as the least populated of the four large Kvarner islands. The island features a mix of the Tramuntana forests, rocky terrain, olive groves, lavender and hidden coves – all of which clearly left a strong impression on the British. The island is known for its hiking and cycling trails, as well as traditional gastronomy and, of course, Cres lamb.

A particularly special attraction are the rare griffon vultures, which nest on the cliffs above the sea. In the settlement of Beli, there is also a visitor centre and recovery centre for these special natural “hygienists” that we must carefully protect.

World.title: Australian With Croatian Roots Runs 827 km Along Croatian Coast
World.content:
September the 7th, 2026 – An Australian with Croatian roots has run a staggering 827 km along the Croatian coast in honour of his late grandfather and to raise awareness about a rare disease.

Australian ultra-marathon runner Aydan Marko Papac from Melbourne has completed one of the most demanding sporting feats of his career. It’s one that few would dare attempt: 827 kilometres of the Croatian coastline, from the lighthouse in Savudrija to Punta Oštro on Prevlaka. Morski reports that it was a feat of sheer endurance, Croatian solidarity and humanity, dedicated to his late grandfather Jandro and to raising awareness of the dreadful Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

Aydan set off from Savudrija on the 24th of August at 05:00, with the ambitious goal of running the entire Croatian coast in a mere ten days. Ahead of him lay 827 kilometres, which implied over 80 kilometres of running every day. That is almost two marathons daily, in the intense Croatian summer heat, plagued with fatigue, pain and with very minimal recovery time.

As he approached Zadar, Aydan’s body began to show the consequences of effort pushed beyond human limits. Due to severe dehydration and significant sodium loss, he had no choice but to stop and receive medical help before he could safely continue, losing more than a full day of running in the process. For most people, that would have been reason enough to give up. For Aydan, it became just another obstacle he was determined to overcome in order to finish the ten-day challenge.

After passing through Dubrovnik on the final stretch, Aydan reached Prevlaka and finally Punta Oštro, the southernmost tip of Croatia, on Thursday, the 3rd of September. With his own feet, he connected the westernmost and southernmost points of the Croatian coast and completed more than 800 kilometres. At the finish line, emotions, hugs, tears of joy and the Croatian flag best showed how much this journey meant to him, his family and the people who supported him along the way.

raising awareness of the devastating Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)

Behind the sporting challenge there was a much deeper story from the very beginning. Aydan dedicated the endeavour to the memory of his grandfather Jandro Bilić, who suffered from a rare and severe neurodegenerative prion disease called Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD). Aydan turned his personal loss into a humanitarian mission: through running, to raise awareness of the disease, support those affected and their families, and connect his Australian homeland with Croatia, the country of his family’s roots. Alongside him throughout this exhausting journey was his wife Georgia, his greatest personal support, as well as family, friends, coaches, cameramen and members of the support team: Jack Colletta (team leader), Ben Cherry (physiotherapist / medical support) and Ramsen Kunda (logistics leader). His journey was also followed by his mother Ana (originally from Tomislavgrad), father Smiljan (originally from Stolac) and sister Mimi. The expedition was filmed by Australian filmmaker Rhidian Scott-Towers of Fourth Lane Media, who will produce a documentary about this brave initiative.

dubrovnik refused to let him run alone

A particularly emotional part of the challenge took place in the Dubrovnik area, where local triathletes and runners joined Aydan. On a stretch of approximately ten kilometres, from Zaton to the viewpoint above Dubrovnik, the following athletes ran with him: Željko Cota, Zoran Ateljević, Davorin Krešić, Igor Krmek, Marin Desnica (all from Triathlon Club Dubrovnik or Hybrid Team Dubrovnik) and Jasmin Husejnović. Zoran Ateljević did not stop there, he rejoined Aydan and ran a full 25 kilometres with him from the Dr. Franjo Tuđman Bridge to Cavtat. Later, Elvis Jelčić and Vasily Belousov also joined the Australian team.

A major role in connecting Aydan’s team with the Dubrovnik running community was played by Alen Bošković, Secretary General of the Dubrovnik Sports Community and Director of Du Motion. After direct communication and a request from the Majestic Film organisational team and ICAN representatives, Bošković helped gather and coordinate local athletes so that Aydan would not be alone in the dark during the final kilometres. It was a moment that best showed what sport can mean, people who may not even have known Aydan beforehand came out onto the road and shared part of his burden with him. Steve Ravić, Director of PR and organisation for all needs in Croatia, said: “When I witnessed it, I felt the emotion like in the film ‘Rocky’, when the city joined him to lift him up. In the last 30 kilometres there were even moments when Aydan could barely walk. It was hard to watch. At the moment he continued, a black dog appeared out of nowhere and followed him all the way to the very end.”

an official reception in dubrovnik

Dubrovnik was the last major city stop before the final stretch through Konavle towards Prevlaka near the Montenegrin border. Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković greeted Aydan via video message, supported the organisation of the reception and congratulated him on the achievement. Due to official duties the mayor unfortunately could not attend in person. The City of Dubrovnik was officially represented by Deputy Mayor Velibor Puzović and Ana Hrnić, the official authorised to temporarily perform the duties of Head of the Administrative Department for Tourism and Sport.

Puzović congratulated Aydan, emphasising that such a feat requires not only exceptional physical fitness but also enormous mental strength and perseverance, and particularly highlighted the value of linking a sporting challenge with a humanitarian message and the memory of his late grandfather. The City of Dubrovnik expressed pride that Dubrovnik hosted Aydan on the last major city stage of his journey. Frano Soldo, a friend of Steve Ravić and owner of Hard Rock Cafe Dubrovnik, kindly hosted the team inside the Old Town.

an enormous organisational effort

A challenge of this magnitude was not just about running. Behind Aydan and his immediate support team there was an extensive multi-day organisation process that began even before his arrival in Croatia and before the official start of the project. The Majestic Film team was involved from the very beginning and started organising and coordinating key elements in advance – communication with cities and local authorities, institutions, media and journalists, sports and running clubs, local contacts, and people who needed to provide support along the entire route.

An important organisational, communication and media role was played by the Majestic Film team, led by Steve Ravić, CEO of Majestic Film and President of ICAN – International Croatian Artists Network. Ravić and the team worked before Aydan’s arrival on building the necessary network of contacts and support and coordinated communication with local authorities, cities, institutions, offices, media, journalists and other relevant partners along the route. During the challenge itself this coordination continued day by day, depending on Aydan’s progress and changes to the route, and included the organisation of media activities, support from sports clubs and runners, and official meetings, including the final communication and reception in the City of Dubrovnik.

Vesna Trokter, as part of the Majestic Film organisational team and ICAN representative, was involved in the project even before the start of the run and was responsible for coordination with the media, runners, running and sports clubs and local contacts. It was through her communication in the Dubrovnik area that cooperation was established with Alen Bošković, after which Dubrovnik runners and triathletes joined Aydan on the final kilometres.

Petra Antolić, Head of Sponsorship and Public Relations at Majestic Film, was also involved before the start of the challenge and actively worked on PR, distribution of information and materials, communication with institutions and the media, and coordination of activities related to Aydan’s arrival and his attempt to set a world record.

In this way Majestic Film did not act only as media support during the run, but from the very beginning was one of the main organisational and communication drivers of the project in Croatia, working on preparations even before Aydan’s arrival and continuing coordination until he reached the finish line on Prevlaka.

Support for Aydan’s mission was also provided by the Central State Office for Croats Abroad and the Croatian Heritage Foundation, including their branch in Pula. In Pula, after the first stage of more than 90 kilometres, he was welcomed by Barbara Buršić, head of the Pula branch of the Croatian Heritage Foundation.

more than a record

At the end of this journey the numbers say a lot: 827 kilometres, ten days of almost continuous movement, several times more than 100 kilometres in a single day, and the entire Croatian coast behind his back. But the numbers do not say everything. They do not speak of the pain and fatigue. They do not speak of the kilometres when the body wants to stop and the mind has to find a reason for one more step. They do not speak of the wife waiting by the roadside, nor of the mother who holds her breath every time he gets up, nor of the family members and team, the proud father and sister who hide the tension they feel in difficult moments, nor of the people who run beside him or the strangers who cheer him on as he passes through their town.

They also do not speak of the work behind the scenes – the calls, messages, emails, arrangements, media coordination and the people who, even before his arrival in Croatia, began building the network of support that accompanied him all the way to the south of the country.

And above all, they do not say enough about the reason Aydan set out, and that is for Grandpa Jandro.

World.title: Significant Weather Change Coming to Croatia
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – A drastic weather change is on the cards for Croatia, bringing relief from oppressive, scorching temperatures.

Index reports that Croatia is currently under the influence of an anticyclone that is bringing clear, stable and hot weather with an inflow of dry air from northern Africa. It won’t last long, however, as a major change is approaching next week. While three tropical cyclones are currently moving across the Pacific, driven by El Niño, and the Atlantic hurricane season is lagging, a deep cyclone between Iceland and Great Britain is slowly shifting eastwards and will affect the weather in continental Europe.

the genoa cyclone

A ridge of high pressure over Scandinavia, connected to the anticyclone over central Europe, extends all the way to northern Africa and the Black Sea. However, a cyclone from the Atlantic will descend towards the North Sea, and its surge of cold and unstable air over western and central Europe will be blocked by the Alps. The jet stream that will bypass the Alps on the western side will trigger the rapid development of a new cyclone in the Gulf of Genoa. That Genoa cyclone, together with the jet stream and a cold front, will begin to influence the weather in Croatia from the middle of next week.

showers, thunderstorms and a significant pressure drop is looming

Before the front actually arrives, due to southerly and south-westerly flow, a strong jugo (sirocco) will blow. The inflow of moisture will further intensify the feeling of sultriness. According to current forecast models, the cold front will affect the northwestern inland areas as well as the northern and central Adriatic during the night from Wednesday to Thursday. During Thursday it will spread across the whole country. The front will be accompanied by thunderstorms, showers and rain, along with strong, locally stormy winds. After the front passes, a strong, locally stormy bora will start blowing in the northern Adriatic. Air temperatures inland will drop by 12 to 15 degrees, and on the Adriatic and in the coastal areas by 8 to 10 degrees.

there’s still a few more days of heat to go

Before the major weather change, we can still expect a few more days of heat. Moderate heatwave warnings from the DHMZ (Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service) have been issued for today, tomorrow and Tuesday. Today it will be sunny and hot with a weak north-westerly wind, while on the Adriatic the maestral will blow. Towards the end of the day and during the night there may be a weak bura in the Velebit coastal area. The DHMZ has issued a heatwave warning for the Adriatic that will last until the middle of the week. Sea temperatures are between 25 and 28 degrees.

On Monday and Tuesday predominantly sunny, warm and hot weather continues. Morning temperatures inland will be around 17°C and on the Adriatic around 23°C. Maximum daytime temperatures inland will range from 30 to 31°C, while on the Adriatic they will reach around 34°C, with a weak to moderate maestral.

On Wednesday the jugo will start blowing, and daytime temperatures will still be high, hovering around 32°C inland and up to 35°C on the Adriatic and islands. In the evening and during the night a gradual increase in cloud cover is expected from the northwest, along with the arrival of the cold front.

World.title: Goodbye Toll Booths: Croatia introducing Crolibertas
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – Croatia is set to introduce Crolibertas early next year as the country finally bids farewell to toll booths.

Poslovni reports that as of the beginning of March 2027, Croatia will abandon the system of toll booths and introduce a fully electronic toll collection system called Crolibertas. Croatia is preparing for a “traffic revolution” that should permanently erase the images of kilometre-long queues in front of toll booths during the summer months. With planned implementation starting on the 1st of March 2027, a new, fully electronic toll collection system named Crolibertas is coming into force. This will consign to history the model of stopping, taking a ticket and paying on exit from the motorway, replacing it with a free-flow traffic system.

It is important to emphasise straight away that, despite the digitalisation, Croatia is not introducing vignettes along the lines of Slovenia or Austria. Tolls will continue to be charged according to the distance travelled and the vehicle category, meaning drivers will pay only for the distance they actually travel on the motorway. The main change lies in the technology and method of collection, which will be automated, faster and more efficient, with the aim of reducing congestion, shortening travel times and cutting harmful emissions caused by stop-start driving.

how it will work

The new system will operate on the basis of so-called “Multi-Lane Free Flow” (MLFF) technology. Instead of the existing toll plazas, portals equipped with cameras and sensors will be installed along the entire motorway network. The system will rely on a combination of two proven technologies: Automatic Licence Plate Recognition (ALPR), which will be the primary solution for light vehicles such as passenger cars and motorcycles and DSRC technology, i.e. communication via the existing ENC devices.

Drivers of light vehicles will have a choice: they can register in the system and link their licence plate to a valid payment method (such as a bank card), or they can continue using an ENC device as before. However, for heavy goods vehicles weighing more than 3.5 tonnes, the use of an ENC device will be mandatory. This ensures that all traffic, regardless of vehicle type, can pass without stopping.

what tourists and foreign drivers need to do

For tourists and foreign nationals, who make up a significant portion of summer traffic, advance preparation will be key. In order to use the motorways smoothly, they will need to register their vehicle in the Crolibertas system in advance. This can be done in several ways: via the central internet portal or mobile app (the most recommended option, so everything can be sorted out before setting off). For those who do not do this in advance, rapid registration will be available on special lanes at motorway entrances (at the locations of the current toll plazas), as well as at physical sales points such as HAC offices or petrol stations.

To avoid any delays, drivers are strongly advised to complete registration online. Special attention should be paid to the accuracy of the entered licence plate data and the validity of the linked payment method, as even the smallest error can lead to charging problems and potential fines.

existing enc users

Existing ENC device users will not need to buy new ones. They will be able to continue using their devices, but with one key change: it will be mandatory to link the existing ENC device to the vehicle’s licence plate.

associated costs and coverage

Regarding prices, Croatian Motorways (HAC) say that the introduction of the new system itself should not lead to an increase in tolls. A new tariff study is being prepared that could introduce more flexible charging models, for example lower prices for travel outside peak periods, which would further relieve traffic. The single electronic toll collection system will cover the entire motorway network in Croatia, including the sections managed by the concessionaires Bina-Istra and Autocesta Zagreb-Macelj. This means drivers will need only one single system for the whole country.

World.title: Croatian Government: New Package of Measures Coming Soon
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – The Croatian Government is currently preparing to present a new autumn package of measures, with nuclear energy part of the discussion.

Croatia has taken a new step towards the possible construction of a nuclear power plant. Ana Blaskovic reports for Poslovni that on Friday, the Croatian Government tasked the Ministry of Economy with launching a structured information procedure and talks with potential suppliers of nuclear technologies and partner countries. Concrete and comparable information will be requested from them on available technologies, technical characteristics and economic conditions.

The process is currently non-binding and does not represent a decision to build a power plant, the government emphasises. However, among the technologies that will be considered are small modular and advanced modular reactors. After the talks, the Ministry will consolidate the collected data and submit a report to the Government. Prime Minister Andrej Plenković announced that at the next session, the government will present the autumn package of measures to mitigate the consequences of the energy crisis for the general public and the economy. The package comes after inflation accelerated to 4.1 percent in August, primarily due to the rise in energy prices, which increased by 17.4 percent on an annual basis.

The government currently expects the upcoming autumn measures to mitigate the impact of energy price increases caused by the crisis still going on over in the Middle East. In addition, through amendments to the Crafts Act, those with crafts will be somewhat financially relieved as chamber contributions will be reduced from two to 1.5 percent of the basic personal allowance, and a novelty is the introduction of status innovations such as the institute of family crafts.

World.title: Estonian tennis player Mark Lajal gets death threats after tournament loss
World.content:
Estonia's top tennis player Mark Lajal received abusive messages and death threats, some to his own phone, following a tournament defeat Delfi reported .

The messages came following his semifinals loss at the ATP Challenger 75 tournament in Manacor, Spain, held at the Rafa Nadal Academy on Mallorca, and the player said they were from sports bettors unhappy about losing money.

Lajal, currently ranked 152nd in the world, shared screenshots of messages he had received aftermath of his semi-final defeat, including from those who had obtained his personal phone number.

The screenshots were in English and included the message:"I really but really hope you will get cancer including your family as well. I hope you will see then [sic] suffer."

Another screenshot Lajal posted read "Look, you son of a b*tch, you're a f*cking loser. I hate you and you must die. You must die, you f*cking son of a b*tch. You and your family must die. You b*stard. I want to kill you."

"Know, we are going to talk, you know what you are doing and you are not dumb as you want people to know you, that's why I'm going to kill all your family," a third message stated.

Lajal, 23, said the abusive and threatening messages had come primarily from disgruntled sports bettors who had lost money on the outcome, and added while he would not normally post on the topic, the messages had gone too far.

"Sometimes these days happen, you lose, but then you get on your phone and somehow people have gotten your number and are calling and texting death threats," he explained, noting the threats and abuse had been directed against his family as well as personally against him after losing.

The player noted abuse like this is the lot of many top players, but questioned the trade-off between this and the big money that sports betting involves: "At the end of the day, ATP keeps accepting all this money from betting platforms, but at what cost?" he noted.

"Gambling addiction is a real issue and I hope these people find and get the help they need," Lajal concluded.

Lajal went through qualifying at the Mallorca event, and defeated Nicolai Budkov Kjaer, a Norwegian player with Estonian roots, 6-3, 6-1 The next round, the quarterfinals, saw him defeat Spanish player Alejo Sanchez Quileze again in straight sets, 6-2, 6-3.

The winning streak came to an end however with a 7-6 (7), 5-7 defeat to France's Felix Balshaw (ATP 252) in the semi final, despite the Estonian initially leading the second set 4-1.

The entire encounter lasted two hours and 10 minutes and Balshaw, 20, will face Spanish player Inaki Montes-De La Torre (ATP 274) in the final.

Other top tennis players who have recently reported receiving death threats and abusive messages include Italy's Matteo Berettini and Panna Udvardy of Hungary.

World.title: Five injured in accident at Estonian Defense Forces central training grounds
World.content:
A serious accident occurred Monday at the Estonian Defense Forces' Central Training Area near Tapa, injuring five people, ERR has learned.

According to a press release from the Estonian Defense Forces Headquarters, an accident occurred during test firing of 120 mm mortar ammunition, injuring five active-duty members of the Scouts Battalion.

"During today's test firing of 120 mm mortar ammunition, excess pressure developed inside the weapon, causing the barrel to rupture. Five active-duty service members near the weapon were injured. One of them was more seriously injured," Scouts Battalion commander Lt. Col. Madis Koosa said in the press release.

The injured service members were examined by medics at the scene and taken to a hospital for further evaluation. Their next of kin have been notified.

The Military Police and the Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS) have launched an investigation to establish the details and circumstances of the incident.
