World.title: Tim Cone unfazed as Gilas Pilipinas heads to Asian Games off blowout losses
World.content:
Tim Cone shoulders the blame as Gilas Pilipinas falls to South Korea by an average of 26.5 points in their two tune-up games ahead of the Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – A pair of blowout losses do not bode well for Gilas Pilipinas’ title defense prospects in the Asian Games, but head coach Tim Cone played down growing fears.

Instead, Cone shouldered the blame after the Philippines fell to South Korea by an average of 26.5 points in their two tune-up games, which formed part of both teams’ preparations for the quadrennial showpiece to be hosted in Nagoya, Japan.

The visiting Filipinos first absorbed an 81-55 defeat to the Koreans on Friday, September 4, then suffered a 69-42 rout on Sunday, September 6.

“We obviously couldn’t approach their level of execution and knowledge of each other,” Cone said of Korea. “These losses weren’t on the players, [they were] on us as a coaching staff.”

Cohesion continues to be a work in progress as almost half of this national team features multiple Gilas Pilipinas first-timers, including Adrian Nocum, Sedrick Barefield, Jerrick Ahanmisi, Zavier Lucero, and Brandon Bates.

The limited preparation time is also a factor, as the Nationals have only been together for around two weeks.

Moreover, the squad remains without Justin Brownlee, the hero of the 2023 championship crew, as the naturalized star has yet to confirm his Asian Games participation owing to injuries that have kept him out of action for over a month.

“We haven’t figured out how to best use the skills of our guys…yet. But me and our staff will be better, and we’ll be better in helping our players prepare for what’s ahead,” said Cone.

For Cone, his wards will have their chance to answer back when it counts.

“No need to panic,” he said.

Bunched in Group C, the Philippines will open its title-retention bid against Bahrain on Friday, September 11, before it tangles with Kazakhstan and China on September 12 and 14, respectively.

The Filipinos need a top-two finish for a sure spot in the quarterfinals. – Rappler.com

World.title: PhilWeb’s multibillion bet on JKS gaming tech triggers PSE suspension
World.content:
Fresh off Lance Gokongwei's P2-billion capital injection and appointment as chairman, PhilWeb is betting big on a multibillion-peso gaming tech investment that could define its turnaround

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) will suspend trading in PhilWeb Corporation starting Tuesday, September 8, after the gaming technology firm disclosed a multibillion investment in JKS Tech Solutions Inc.

PhilWeb said on Monday, September 7, that it and wholly owned subsidiary PhilWeb Capital Corporation had signed subscription agreements covering a combined 10.73 million Common B shares of JKS at P394 apiece.

PhilWeb itself will subscribe to 3.41 million JKS shares worth about P1.34 billion, while PhilWeb Capital will take another 7.32 million shares.

The scale is what makes this investment significant. As of June 30, PhilWeb reported just P548.46 million in total assets against P741.95 million in liabilities. This left the company with negative stockholders’ equity of P193.48 million.

Those figures, however, came before the completion of JG Summit tycoon Lance Gokongwei’s P2-billion capital infusion into PhilWeb.

Even before the big boost of capital that Gokongwei provided, PhilWeb had already begun improving operationally, returning to profit in the first half with net income of P60.97 million, compared with a P41.77-million loss a year earlier.

The PSE said the JKS deal falls under its rules covering substantial acquisitions and reverse takeovers and will suspend PhilWeb shares beginning 9 am Tuesday while waiting for the company’s required comprehensive disclosure.

Under PSE rules, the substantial acquisition provision applies when a listed company or its subsidiary acquires a direct or indirect interest in an unlisted company equivalent to at least 10% of the listed firm’s total book value. PhilWeb’s P4.23-billion investment blows past that threshold: it is roughly 7.7 times the company’s entire P548.5-million asset base as of end-June, before the Gokongwei capital infusion was factored in.

Rappler has asked PhilWeb for its comment on the deal and suspension. This story will be updated once a response is received.

Who is JKS?

PhilWeb described JKS as a “Philippine B2B technology, platform and digital infrastructure company serving licensed mid-market operators in the digital entertainment sector.”

Beyond PhilWeb’s relatively dry description of JKS as a technology and digital infrastructure company, Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) records reveal more about what the company actually does.

JKS is the PAGCOR-accredited gaming system administrator behind Epic Game, a regulated online gaming platform. Its approved offerings span traditional and electronic bingo, electronic casino games, sports betting, specialty games, and numeric games.

A two-way investment

Money and shares are moving in both directions. In a separate disclosure on Monday, PhilWeb said JKS agreed to buy 81.38 million PhilWeb treasury shares for P16.50 each, paying a total of about P1.34 billion. The shares to be acquired represent around 4.85% of PhilWeb’s issued and outstanding shares, giving JKS a meaningful stake in the listed company once the transaction is completed.

The P1.34 billion that JKS will pay PhilWeb almost exactly matches PhilWeb’s own P1.34-billion direct subscription to JKS.

PhilWeb Capital Corporation, meanwhile, will subscribe to a much larger P2.88 billion worth of JKS shares. Monday’s disclosures did not specify how the PhilWeb subsidiary would fund that investment.

Nevertheless, PhilWeb has raised significant fresh capital in recent months, which could help fund its latest multibillion deal. In June, Gokongwei agreed to personally invest about P2.03 billion in the company through common and redeemable preferred shares priced at P8 apiece. PhilWeb said at the time that the money would strengthen its capital base and give it greater financial flexibility, including for “expansion opportunities and investments.”

Gokongwei acquired 159.53 million common shares on August 27 and was appointed PhilWeb chairman on the same day, replacing Crisanto Roy Alcid, who remained a director. – Rappler.com

World.title: DepEd seeks more funds as ARAL gets zero in proposed 2027 budget
World.content:
BUDGET BRIEFING. Education Secretary Sonny Angara presents the proposed P976-billion budget of the Department of Education and its attached agencies during a House appropriations committee hearing on September 7, 2026.

The Department of Education is requesting an additional P145 billion in 2027 to fund the ARAL Program, hire new teachers, build classrooms, and improve students' health, among others

MANILA, Philippines – The Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program has no allocation in the proposed 2027 budget, according to Education Secretary Sonny Angara, potentially hurting efforts of the Department of Education (DepEd) to address the learning crisis in the country.

“There’s a zero allotment for this under the 2027 budget,” Angara told the House appropriations committee on Monday, September 7, when asked regarding the proposed allocation for the national learning intervention program next year.

The ARAL Program, institutionalized through Republic Act (RA) No. 12028 in October 2024, seeks to help public school students who struggle in reading, mathematics, and science.

With the program’s funding scrapped in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), the DepEd presented its “wishlist” to lawmakers on Monday. Part of the department’s request is P15.98 billion to carry out the ARAL Program in 2027.

In the 2026 national budget, the program was allocated P8.9 billion.

“The program has good results because out of the 6.67 million students that entered the ARAL Program, we saw at the end of the [previous] school year (2025-2026) that there were 4.5 million fewer struggling readers, with 2.5 million students improving to grade-level reading,” Angara said in a mix of English and Filipino.

So far, the DepEd has only rolled out learning interventions for reading, according to Angara. He hopes they can include sessions for mathematics and science.

Ruby Bernardo, Alliance of Concerned Teachers national chairperson, expressed dismay over the possible zero budget for the ARAL Program. She also stressed that remediation and learning recovery efforts must already be removed from teachers’ load.

“Kung mananatili ‘yan sa teachers natin, malaki ang epekto niya sa learning recovery ng mga bata. Kung walang pondo, wala ring maha-hire na external tutors,” Bernardo said in a chance interview. (If the task would remain with the teachers, it would have a huge effect on the learning recovery of children. If there’s no funding, there would be no hiring of external tutors.)

Angara sought intervention from lawmakers as RA 12028 is specific that teachers are only entitled to overload pay if they exceed six hours of teaching.

This is amid the unresolved issue of whether teachers should be compensated for handling ARAL tutor work regardless of teaching load.

Angara said that for now, the DepEd is studying the possibility of giving food allowance in cash, if allowed by the Commission on Audit. The agency is also eyeing to include in the six-hour teaching load some teacher-related tasks, such as the time spent on peer-mentoring sessions or advising students.

In a message to Rappler, Karol Mark Yee, executive director of the Second Congressional Commission on Education, said he hopes that Congress will fund the ARAL Program as it is an “urgent need,” given that there are millions of struggling readers.

But Yee also noted that there must be a thorough review of the DepEd’s utilization of the nearly P9-billion ARAL Program funding this year.

Other budget requests

In the 2027 NEP, the DepEd, including its attached agencies, may get P976 billion. However, the education department received P1 trillion in the 2026 budget.

In total, the DepEd requested from the House appropriations committee P145.19 billion in additional funds, while its attached agencies are seeking P1.74 billion more.

The additional funds being sought include P33.53 billion for new personnel. According to Angara, the proposed 2027 budget does not have an allocation for the hiring of new teachers.

Angara also lamented the proposed P11-billion budget for the school-based feeding program, a significant decrease from the P25.7 billion in the 2026 budget.

He explained that the feeding cycle might have to be shortened from 180 days to 120 days, and the lower budget would prevent the DepEd from offering universal feeding to all Grade 1 pupils.

Measures to address school violence, such as strengthening school safety and expanding access to mental health services, are also covered by the budget requests.

When asked how the budget cuts could affect the DepEd’s reforms, Angara told reporters after the seven-hour budget hearing, “It would slow it down a little bit, but we are hoping for a restoration of some of the items.”

World.title: Alex Eala full of gratitude despite painful US Open exit
World.content:
BELOVED. The Philippines' Alexandra Eala acknowledges the crowd after losing her third-round match against Iva Jovic of the United States in the 2026 US Open.

Alex Eala says it is a “real privilege to experience” playing on tennis’ biggest stages and receiving overwhelming fan support even as her US Open run comes to a heartbreaking end

MANILA, Philippines – Even in the face of one of her most painful defeats, Alex Eala somehow still radiates gratitude.

Eala chooses to look at the silver lining after her US Open campaign came to a heartbreaking end following a stinging 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 loss to close friend Iva Jovic of the United States in the third round on Sunday, September 5 (Monday, September 6, Manila time).

The defeat denied Eala a chance to match her best Grand Slam showing — a fourth-round run in the Wimbledon Championships in July — but the Filipina world No. 18 relished her debut at the famed Arthur Ashe Stadium, buoyed by a passionate crowd rallying behind her.

“It’s indescribable to sum up the support and how it makes me feel in just a few words. It’s a real privilege to experience this in a lifetime,” said Eala, pausing to fight back tears.

“Playing on Arthur Ashe and feeling the support and being in those environments and learning these lessons and fighting and doing what I love, I’m really happy. I’m really lucky to have these opportunities, to have these people support me, and to be working hard, to be able to work hard, and to be able to live this life how I am living it.”

Eala proved she deserved to play at the world’s largest tennis stadium as she engaged world No. 14 Jovic in a three-hour thriller that kept those in attendance on the edge of their seats.

Swept by Jovic in both of their two previous encounters, Eala finally took a set from the American and even built a 4-2 lead in the decider before she ran out of gas, losing four of the last five games.

Although a breakthrough win against Jovic slipped through her fingers, Eala has every reason to hold her head high after battling until the final point.

“What I’ve learned tonight, I have yet to process. But I think that what I know for sure is that I left everything out there,” Eala said.

“I fought through the ups and downs. There were moments where I wasn’t playing so good, and moments where I was playing really good. So, what I know for a fact is that I fought. So, I’m happy with that.”

Eala gets a two-week break before she returns to action at the Singapore Open, which will run from September 21 to 27.

Then, from Singapore, the 21-year-old will fly to Japan for the Asian Games, where she is billed as one of the Philippines’ top gold-medal prospects following her bronze finish in the 2023 edition in China.

“I love playing and competing with the Philippine team,” said Eala. “I think it’s a really fun environment, and I love being with the team.” – Rappler.com

World.title: Rain from southwest monsoon to persist in second week of September
World.content:
Zambales could be the most affected province in the next 24 hours, says PAGASA on Monday afternoon, September 7

MANILA, Philippines – The southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to trigger rain in Luzon and the Visayas in the second week of September, raising the risk of more floods and landslides.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Monday afternoon, September 7, that Zambales could experience heavy to intense rain in the next 24 hours.

A handful of provinces may have moderate to heavy rain within 48 hours, but beyond that period, nearly 30 areas — including Metro Manila — could already be affected by significant rainfall.

Here is PAGASA’s 72-hour rainfall outlook as of 5 pm on Monday:

Monday afternoon, September 7, to Tuesday afternoon, September 8

Heavy to intense rain (100-200 millimeters): Zambales

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Pangasinan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, Antique

Tuesday afternoon, September 8, to Wednesday afternoon, September 9

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Isabela, Aurora, Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro

Wednesday afternoon, September 9, to Thursday afternoon, September 10

Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Occidental Mindoro

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Nueva Vizcaya, Quirino, Aurora, Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, Laguna, Quezon, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, Palawan, Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, Albay, Catanduanes, Aklan, Antique

On Monday evening, other areas in Luzon and Western Visayas not mentioned above are expected to see scattered rain and thunderstorms, while the rest of the Visayas may have isolated rain showers or thunderstorms, still due to the southwest monsoon.

All affected areas should stay on alert for floods and landslides.

For now, there are no low pressure areas (LPAs) or potential tropical cyclones being monitored inside or outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).

But PAGASA said two LPAs might form during the week, with one of them possibly east of the Philippines and the other located west of the country. The latter could have a high chance of developing into a tropical cyclone.

The weather bureau expects two or three tropical cyclones to develop within or enter PAR in September. The next three local tropical cyclone names are Queenie, Rosal, and Samuel. – Rappler.com

World.title: Martin Romualdez arrested over P7.44-B plunder case but remains in hospital
World.content:
(3rd UPDATE) The former House speaker may be detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas – the designated detention center for flood control-related cases

MANILA, Philippines – Leyte 1st District Representative and former House speaker Martin Romualdez was arrested Monday, September 7, over his P7.44-billion plunder case, but would remain in hospital confinement at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City.

After the Office of the Ombudsman filed a plunder case against Romualdez and his co-accused — former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co, Joselyn Serenio, and Felicito Guevarra — the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division issued a warrant of arrest and hold departure orders against them past 5 pm Monday.

Romualdez allegedly received P7.44 billion in kickbacks from Co, who is at large.

On Monday night, Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) chief Juanito Victor “Jonvic” Remulla and Philippine National Police chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez served the warrant against Romualdez, who has been confined at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center since 4 pm.

Remulla told Rappler they had already served the warrant and arrested Romualdez. He said the former speaker is suffering from a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and anxiety attacks.

The DILG chief added that they will check on Romualdez every day until he’s ready to be transferred to the Sandiganbayan for the return of his warrant.

“We assure you, he cannot hide behind his wealth…. Dadalhin namin siya sa Payatas sa tamang panahon…. Patas ang laban dito (We will bring him to Payatas at the proper moment. This is a fair fight),” said Remulla.

Sandiganbayan 3rd Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma earlier told reporters that at around 6 pm on Monday, Romualdez filed a manifestation for hospital confinement and an urgent motion for continued hospital confinement under custody.



Pulma also clarified that the 3rd Division ordered the Sandiganbayan sheriff to implement the warrant.

“If there are concerns regarding the accused’s medical condition, it is only the Court that can determine whether such condition affects the implementation of the warrant,” Pulma said.

“If there are medical concerns, these should be properly documented and brought to the attention of the Court. Until the Court orders otherwise, the warrant remains in force and must be implemented,” he added.

The plunder case against Romualdez makes him one of the highest officials to be charged over the multi-billion flood control anomaly.

“Based on our investigation, Romualdez allegedly received kickbacks around 15 times from Co’s staff, from September 2022 to 2025. That’s for the P2-billion monthly quota or collections Romualdez imposed on Co,” the Ombudsman said in Filipino.

“Serenio received the cash delivery in the lawmaker’s different houses and properties. Romualdez used nearly P5 billion from these kickbacks to establish shell or dummy companies like Golden Pheasant Holdings Corporation, Braavos Holdings Opc, and Valiant Consolidated Resources, Inc.,” it added.

According to the Ombudsman, their case against Romualdez and co-accused stands on the evidence and testimonies from several witnesses, including former Department of Public Works and Highways undersecretary Roberto Bernardo and former DPWH Bulacan district engineer Henry Alcantara, among others.

“The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged. Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested,” said the 3rd Division.

Plunder is non-bailable. Romualdez, who is now under police custody, is likely to be detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas — the designated detention center for flood control-related cases. – Rappler.com

World.title: Ilocos Sur town probes dredging near its waters
World.content:
The alleged dredging activity off Barangay Nangalisan in Sta. Lucia, Ilocos Sur, is shown during a municipal inspection on Sept. 7. Town officials inspected the area to determine whether the operation falls within Sta. Lucia’s territorial waters and assess its possible environmental impact. (Photos courtesy of Sta. Lucia LGU)

SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The municipal government of Sta. Lucia said it would not tolerate unauthorized or environmentally harmful dredging within its jurisdiction, citing the need to protect marine ecosystems and the livelihoods of coastal communities.

The statement came after municipal officials inspected a dredging activity off Barangay Nangalisan on Monday, Sept. 7, to determine whether the operation falls within Sta. Lucia’s territorial waters and assess its possible environmental impact.

READ: Pangasinan will do dredging to reduce floods, says governor

Article continues after this 

The initial on-site assessment showed that the dredging site was about 1,933 meters from the identified municipal boundary toward Sabangan, an area under neighboring Sta. Cruz town.

Mayor Joseph Simon Valdez, Vice Mayor Eduardo Toquero, members of the Sangguniang Bayan, barangay officials and representatives from the Municipal Engineering and Assessor’s offices joined the inspection, along with personnel from the police and Bureau of Fire Protection.

The local government said the measurement and site inspection form part of its continuing verification of the dredging operation’s exact location in relation to the boundaries of Sta. Lucia and Sta. Cruz.

Officials also documented conditions in the area and assessed the possible effects of the dredging on the coastal environment.

The municipal government said it would coordinate with concerned government agencies to determine whether the operation complies with environmental laws and other regulations. /mcm

World.title: Loren Legarda praises enactment of stronger free college law
World.content:
Sen. Loren Legarda —Photo from her office

MANILA, Philippines — More students from poor families can now stay in school and finish their education, Sen. Loren Legarda said as she welcomed on Monday the enactment of Republic Act No. 12325, which strengthens the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education.

The new law, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Sept. 4, improves the tertiary education subsidy (TES) by directing assistance more deliberately toward the poorest students and recognizing that the cost of education goes far beyond tuition.

“It’s not enough that tuition is free if students have no money for fare to go to school and buy books, and then are short of money to buy food, or are forced to stop to help their families. Free college must mean that a student has a real chance not only to enroll, but to stay in school and graduate,” Legarda said in a mix of Filipino and English in a statement issued on Monday.

Article continues after this 

READ: Marcos signs law expanding aid for college, vocational students

More focus on poor students

Legarda principally sponsored and authored Senate Bill No. 1894, which strengthened Republic Act No. 10931 by making student assistance more responsive to the actual financial burden of pursuing college or technical-vocational education.

Among its key reforms is focusing the subsidy more on students who need government assistance most, particularly senior high school graduates from Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) households who are admitted to qualified higher education or technical-vocational institutions.

The reform addresses a significant gap identified by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom II). Legarda now serves as an Edcom II commissioner, previously serving as its co-chairperson. She was also the chairperson of the Senate Committee on Higher, Technical, and Vocational Education

As Legarda points out, the share of TES beneficiaries from the poorest households fell from 70.73 percent in 2018 to 22.89 percent in 2022. Of 384,388 senior high school graduates from 4Ps households, only 4,746, or 1.23 percent, received TES as first-year beneficiaries in academic year 2024–2025.

Article continues after this 

“The data is clear. Many youths who should get aid first don’t benefit from it. We strengthened the system to make sure that more families in need will get the opportunity to let their children finish. We can’t describe an opportunity as universal if the poorest are the ones who get aid last,” Legarda said.

Regular subsidy reviews

The new law also provides for regular reviews of TES amounts so that it can respond to changes in the actual cost of education.

Article continues after this 

To make tertiary education more inclusive, state universities and colleges, local universities and colleges, and state-run technical-vocational institutions are also required to adopt Equity and Inclusion Plans.

This aims to remove barriers faced by persons with disabilities, students from geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, indigenous peoples, and learners from other disadvantaged backgrounds.

READ: Expanded free college law to help more Filipino youth earn degrees – Dy

The law also establishes the Private Education Assistance Program, which will support qualified students who need financial assistance in private higher education institutions and technical-vocational schools.

Legarda pointed out that the law advances a principle she had been consistently pushing in education policy — that government must look beyond how many students enter school and focus on whether they are actually able to finish.

“We hope to ensure that no Filipino youth will lose the opportunity to get a quality education just because their families lack money. The lack of money should not be a reason for their education to be cut short and their dreams blocked,” she said. /atm

World.title: P48.9M ‘smuggled’ cigarettes seized in Pampanga, 4 men arrested
World.content:
MABALACAT CITY — The police arrested four men for transporting some an estimated P48,955,500 worth of suspected smuggled cigarettes in Barangay Cacutud here shortly after midnight on Monday.

In a statement, the Police Regional Office 3 (PRO3) said the operation which resulted in the arrest was carried out after several days of surveillance operations.

Authorities had received information that a truck was being used to transport and store cases of suspected illicit cigarettes at a secluded location in the city.

Article continues after this 

At around 12:30 a.m., operatives from the Regional Special Operations Group-Regional Intelligence Division 3, Mabalacat City Police Station, and Criminal Investigation and Detection Group Regional Field Unit 3 successfully intercepted the target truck and arrested its driver and three companions.

“A search of the truck led to the discovery of 759 master cases of ‘Modern’ cigarettes — 329 master cases of red packs and 430 master cases of blue packs. The products were observed to have no Bureau of Internal Revenue tax stamps and remain subject to further examination and verification,” the PRO3 said.

PRO3 Director Brig. Gen. Jess Mendez said the impact of the operation went beyond the amount of contraband seized, noting that illicit trade deprives the government of potential revenues that could support public services, puts legitimate businesses at a disadvantage, and allows illegal trade networks to profit at the expense of lawful commerce.

“Keeping these products off the market helps protect consumers, businesses, and the local economy,” he added.

The PRO3 said the recovered items were inventoried in the presence of the arrested individuals and a barangay official.

Article continues after this 

Alternative recording devices were also used during the operation in accordance with existing procedures.

The four arrested individuals and the recovered evidence were brought to the police regional camp for documentation and proper disposition.

Article continues after this 

According to PRO3, it was coordinating with the appropriate government agencies to determine the applicable violations to be filed against the arrested persons and to conduct further examination and verification of the recovered cigarette products. /gsg

World.title: Mark Villar welcomes passage of tougher anti-hospital detention bill
World.content:
Sen. Mark Villar —Photo from his office

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Mark Villar welcomes the Senate’s approval of a bill imposing heavier penalties on hospitals and medical clinics that detain patients or their families because of unpaid medical expenses.

The upper chamber has recently approved Senate Bill No. 1511, or the proposed Enhanced Anti-Hospital Detention Act, on third and final reading with 18 affirmative votes, no negative votes, and one abstention.

The bill seeks to strengthen Republic Act No. 9439, which prohibits hospitals and clinics from preventing patients unable to settle their medical bills immediately from going home.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate passes anti-hospital detention bill

“Hospitals and clinics should not become jails for our countrymen who can’t immediately pay for their bills,” Villar said in Filipino in a statement issued on Monday.

As he pointed out, hospitalization already places families under significant emotional and financial pressure. So they should not be humiliated over unpaid accounts.

Under the proposed law, hospitals and clinics found illegally detaining patients, newborn babies, or the remains of deceased patients would face heavier penalties.

The same provision also applies to patients’ relatives, representatives, and caregivers — preventing a practice known as “palit-ulo,” in which a hospital or clinic requires them to remain at the facility in exchange for the release of their patient.

Article continues after this 

It also prohibits medical facilities from withholding newborns following maternity-related treatment or refusing to release the remains of deceased patients because of unsettled hospital bills.

Under the bill, hospital employees or officers directly responsible for an illegal detention may be fined up to ₱300,000 or imprisoned for up to two years and four months.

Article continues after this 

Hospital directors or officers who create or enforce policies permitting illegal detention may face fines ranging from ₱500,000 to ₱1 million and imprisonment of four to six years.

A medical facility may also lose its license to operate after three violations committed under such a policy.

READ: IN THE KNOW: Anti-Hospital Deposit Law

Villar clarified, however, that the measure would neither cancel legitimate medical debts nor prevent hospitals from collecting unpaid obligations. Instead, it would require healthcare facilities to use legal and humane collection methods.

Patients unable to pay their bills immediately may issue promissory notes supported by legally recognized security or guarantee arrangements. Qualified patients may also obtain guarantee letters from appropriate government agencies.
